parts.prompt: By taking moments about support B, calculate the upward reaction force F₁ at support A while the technician is at the initial position.
workingSteps: Clockwise moment of F₁ about B = F₁ × 4.6.

parts.prompt: Deduce the upward reaction force F₂ at support B.
State qualitatively how the reaction forces at supports A and B change as the technician walks slowly toward the right-hand overhang.
parts.expectedAnswer: As the technician moves toward the overhang, the reaction force at support A decreases and the reaction force at support B increases.
workingSteps: Explain that shifting weight toward support B reduces the anticlockwise moment about B so support A carries less load while support B carries more.

parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum distance past support B that the technician can walk onto the overhang before the plank begins to tip.
workingSteps: At the tipping limit, F₁ = 0; take moments about B: 86 g d_tip = 40 g (1.200).

items.stem: Across a level driving range, a tee on flat ground projects a golf launch-monitor ball with initial speed 38 m s⁻¹ at 52° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a level driving range?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 38 sin 52° = 29.9 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 38 cos 52° = 23.4 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 6.11 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 143 m. Target = 143 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 143 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: During proving-ground tests, a harbour container carrier of mass 1800 kg accelerates along a level straight so a suspended mass indicator deflects by 34° from the vertical, climbs a straight 14° incline at constant speed, negotiates a flat semicircular curve of radius 95 m (coefficient of static friction 0.7), and finally coasts along the semicircle from 18 m s⁻¹ against a constant 470 N resistance toward the berth checkpoint. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg => a = g tan θ.
Obtains 6.62 m s⁻².
Applies μ_s mg = m v_max² / R.
Obtains 25.5 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts resistive work F_res(πR) from initial kinetic energy ½mu².
Obtains 13.0 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: By resolving forces on a suspended mass indicator, calculate the horizontal acceleration when the string deflects by 34°.
Calculate the maximum speed on the flat semicircular road without sliding.
Calculate the speed with which a harbour container carrier reaches the berth checkpoint at the end of the semicircular coast.

items.stem: A $76.0\text{ kg}$ meteorological drop-probe descends vertically through Earth's lower atmosphere ($g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$) following the two-stage velocity–time profile shown before deploying a drogue parachute. At point P, the upward aerodynamic drag is $450\text{ N}$.
items.workedSolution: (a) $W = 745.6\text{ N}$, $F = 295.6\text{ N}$, $a = 3.89 m s⁻²$. (b) Drag grows with speed until equal to weight at terminal velocity and opening the parachute creates an upward resultant force; SUVAT is invalid and total distance equals area under the $v\text{–}t$ curve.

markScheme.criterion: Calculate weight $W = 76.0 \times 9.81 = 746\text{ N}$.
Find downward resultant $F = W - 450 = 296\text{ N}$ and divide by $76.0\text{ kg}$.
Acceleration $= 3.89 m s⁻²$.
L1 (Area 1): As speed grows, upward drag increases, decreasing downward resultant force (mg − D) and acceleration (N2L).
L1 (Area 1): At Q, drag equals constant weight -> zero resultant force -> constant terminal speed (N1L).
L2 (Area 2): Opening drogue parachute raises drag well above weight, producing an upward resultant force and downward deceleration (N2L).
L2 (Area 2): As speed falls, drag decreases until drag equals weight again at a lower constant terminal speed S.
L3 (Area 3): Explains direction stays downwards because deceleration reduces positive downward speed toward vT2 rather than reversing it.
L3 (Area 3): Notes SUVAT equations cannot be used (non-uniform acceleration); distance fallen is found from area under the v–t curve.

parts.prompt: Calculate the downward acceleration of the probe at point P.
workingSteps: Downward resultant force $F = W - D = 296 N$.

parts.prompt: Explain using Newton's laws why the probe's acceleration falls to zero at Q, why opening the drogue parachute at R reduces its speed without reversing its direction of motion, and how to find total distance fallen from the graph.
parts.expectedAnswer: Drag grows with speed until equal to weight at terminal velocity and opening the parachute creates an upward resultant force. During descent from release through P, increasing air drag cuts the downward resultant force $mg - D$ until at Q drag equals weight, giving zero resultant force and constant terminal speed (N1L). Deploying the drogue canopy at R sharply increases area and upward drag above weight, giving an upward resultant force and deceleration (N2L) that slows the downward velocity—it never reverses direction because drag falls back to $mg$ while velocity is still downwards, establishing a lower terminal speed at S. Because acceleration is non-uniform, SUVAT equations are invalid and total distance fallen is found from the area under the $v\text{–}t$ graph.
workingSteps: Area 1 (L1): Drag increases with speed -> downward resultant drops -> at Q drag = weight -> zero acceleration (N1L).
Area 2 (L2): Drogue opens -> drag >> weight -> upward resultant decelerates downward motion -> drag drops until D = mg at lower terminal speed S.
Area 3 (L3): Velocity stays downward (deceleration != upward motion) and distance equals area under v-t curve (SUVAT invalid).

items.stem: A precast concrete stormwater channel of length L = 2.80 m rests horizontally on level ground (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). As shown in the figure, it has a semi-annular cross-section of outer diameter D = 20.0 cm and inner diameter d = 12.0 cm and average density ρ = 2400 kg m⁻³. The component is uniform along its length so its centre of gravity G lies at its midpoint. A portable site winch motor rated at electrical input power 420 W and efficiency 75% is later attached to end B to stand the component vertically upright on end A.
items.workedSolution: (a) A = 0.01005 m², V = A L = 0.02815 m³, m = ρ V = 67.56 kg ≈ 67.6 kg. (b) W = 662.7 N; taking moments about A gives F = W × (x_G / L) = 331.4 N ≈ 331 N. (c) Centre of gravity rises by Δh = 1.400 m, so ΔE_p = m g Δh = 927.8 J ≈ 928 J. (d) Useful power P_out = 0.75 × 420 = 315.0 W, so t = 927.8 / 315.0 = 2.945 s ≈ 2.95 s. (e) density is uniform and negligible work is done against friction or giving kinetic energy to the beam.

markScheme.criterion: Computes semi-annular cross-section A = (π/8)(D² − d²) = 0.01005 m² with cm → m conversion.
Calculates V = A L = 0.02815 m³ and substitutes m = ρ V.
Shows 4 s.f. mass 67.56 kg rounding clearly to 67.6 kg.
Applies principle of moments about A: F × 2.80 = m g × 1.400.
Evaluates minimum lift force F = 331 N (4 s.f. 331.4 N).
Uses centre-of-gravity rise Δh = 1.400 m (not full length L) in ΔE_p = m g Δh.
Obtains work done = 928 J (4 s.f. 927.8 J).
Applies useful power P_out = η P_in = 315.0 W and t = ΔE_p / P_out.
Evaluates minimum hoist time = 2.95 s (4 s.f. 2.945 s).
States valid physical assumption: density is uniform and negligible work is done against friction or giving kinetic energy to the beam.

items.stem: A non-uniform reinforced concrete lintel of length L = 3.20 m rests horizontally on level ground (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). As shown in the figure, it has a rectangular cross-section of width w = 22.0 cm and thickness h = 12.0 cm and average density ρ = 2420 kg m⁻³. Internal reinforcement makes the component non-uniform so its centre of gravity G lies at distance x = 1.41 m from end A (as shown). A overhead workshop crane motor rated at electrical input power 720 W and efficiency 80% is later attached to end B to stand the component vertically upright on end A.
items.workedSolution: (a) A = 0.02640 m², V = A L = 0.08448 m³, m = ρ V = 204.4 kg ≈ 204 kg. (b) W = 2006 N; taking moments about A gives F = W × (x_G / L) = 882.5 N ≈ 882 N. (c) Centre of gravity rises by Δh = 1.408 m, so ΔE_p = m g Δh = 2824 J ≈ 2.82e+3 J. (d) Useful power P_out = 0.80 × 720 = 576.0 W, so t = 2824 / 576.0 = 4.903 s ≈ 4.90 s. (e) electrical heating in the motor windings and friction in the hoist gears dissipate thermal energy to the surroundings.

markScheme.criterion: Calculates cross-section A = 0.02640 m², volume V = 0.08448 m³, and applies m = ρ V.
Shows 4 s.f. mass 204.4 kg confirming 204 kg.
Applies principle of moments about A: F × 3.20 = m g × 1.408.
Evaluates minimum lift force F = 882 N (4 s.f. 882.5 N).
Uses centre-of-gravity rise Δh = 1.408 m (not full length L) in ΔE_p = m g Δh.
Obtains work done = 2.82e+3 J (4 s.f. 2824 J).
Applies useful power P_out = η P_in = 576.0 W and t = ΔE_p / P_out.
Evaluates minimum hoist time = 4.90 s (4 s.f. 4.903 s).
Identifies electrical heating in motor windings and mechanical friction in hoist gears.
Links losses to thermal energy dissipated to the surroundings (electrical heating in the motor windings and friction in the hoist gears dissipate thermal energy to the surroundings).

options.label: A
options.text: Use a swinging pendulum beside the stand and plot h against t so the gradient equals g.
options.distractorRationale: AQA mark schemes reject 'pendulum' for plumb line, and h vs t is curved rather than linear.

options.label: B
options.text: Use a plumb line to align the metre ruler vertically and plot two h over t against t so the gradient equals gravitational field strength independently of initial speed.

options.label: C
options.text: Eyeball the stand vertically and assume the sphere enters Gate 1 with zero velocity.
options.distractorRationale: Visual estimation leaves tilt error, and the sphere already has speed u > 0 at Gate 1.

options.label: D
options.text: Plot h/t² against h because it eliminates gravitational acceleration from the vertical intercept.
options.distractorRationale: h = ut + ½gt² linearizes cleanly as 2h/t = gt + 2u (or h/t = ½gt + u).

items.stem: A student releases a dense steel ball from an electromagnet to a trapdoor switch (RP3) across several heights and plots $h$ against $t^2$. The best-fit straight line has gradient 4.76 m s⁻². Determine the experimental value of $g$.
items.workedSolution: Comparing $h = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ with $y = mx$, the gradient equals $g/2$, so $g = 2 \times 4.76 = 9.52 m s⁻²$.

markScheme.criterion: Calculates $g = 9.52 m s⁻²$.

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a shopping-arcade hanging directional sign bar of total length L = 3.6 m and mass 22 kg hangs horizontally in equilibrium from two light vertical ceiling wires attached at A and B, separated by 2.9 m. Its centre of gravity G lies 2.09 m to the right of attachment A and 0.81 m to the left of attachment B (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Without carrying out a full calculation, which statement correctly compares the tensions in the two wires?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about the centre of gravity G gives T₁ d_A = T₂ d_B, so the wire with the smaller distance to G carries the larger tension: wire B carries the greater tension because the centre of gravity is closer to wire B.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly concludes that wire B carries the greater tension because the centre of gravity is closer to wire B.

options.text: In horizontal equilibrium, wire B carries the greater tension because the centre of gravity is closer to wire B.

options.label: B
options.text: Wire A carries the greater tension because the centre of gravity is farther from wire A.
options.distractorRationale: Reverses the inverse lever-arm relation; the support closer to G bears the larger share of weight.

options.label: C
options.text: Both wires carry identical tension because the bar hangs completely horizontal.
options.distractorRationale: Horizontal equilibrium requires zero net moment, which forces unequal tensions when G is off-centre.

options.label: D
options.text: Neither wire tension depends on the horizontal location of the centre of gravity.
options.distractorRationale: Moment balance directly couples the tension ratio to the distances of G from each wire.

items.stem: Two equal and opposite parallel forces, each of magnitude F = 150 N, are applied to the ends of a submarine hatch locking handbar of length d = 0.48 m, acting perpendicularly to the bar, as illustrated in the diagram. What is the combined mechanical effect of this couple acting alone on the free bar?
items.workedSolution: A rigid body acted on only by this couple experiences zero resultant force but a non-zero resultant torque causing rotational motion.

markScheme.criterion: A rigid body acted on only by this couple experiences zero resultant force but a non-zero resultant torque causing rotational motion.

items.stem: Sliding at constant velocity down a straight haulage incline of slope length 25 m and vertical drop 7 m, a mining equipment skid has weight 1360 N. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1360 × 7 = 9.52 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 381 N. Target = 381 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 7/25 and zero net force to obtain 381 N (D).

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a laboratory optical-rail hinged wall shelf is a uniform horizontal rod of length L = 1.8 m and mass 4 kg smoothly hinged to a vertical wall at O. A rectangular sign of mass 9.5 kg hangs so that its centre of gravity acts 1.4 m from O. A taut support wire joins the outer end of the rod to the wall at an angle of 54° above the horizontal rod (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Moments about O give T = 113.8 N ≈ 114 N. (b) Horizontal balance: R_x = T cos θ = 66.92 N ≈ 66.9 N. (c) Vertical balance: R_y = W_total − T sin θ = 40.33 N ≈ 40.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Writes full moment balance about hinge O including both rod and sign moments with T sin θ.
Evaluates T = 113.8 N (114 N) showing agreement with 1.1e+2 N.
Applies horizontal equilibrium R_x = T cos θ.
R_x = 66.9 N away from the wall.
Applies vertical equilibrium R_y = W_total − T sin θ.
R_y = 40.3 N upwards.

workingSteps: Clockwise moment about O = (4 × 0.9 + 9.5 × 1.4) × 9.81 = 165.8 N m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the horizontal component of the force exerted by hinge O on the rod.
workingSteps: Horizontal equilibrium: R_x = T cos 54° = 113.8 × cos 54° = 66.92 N ≈ 66.9 N away from the wall.

parts.prompt: Calculate the vertical component of the force exerted by hinge O on the rod.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium: R_y = W − T sin 54° = 40.33 N ≈ 40.3 N upwards.

items.stem: In Required Practical 4 on a nichrome alloy wire of length $(2.60 \pm 0.002)$ m, orthogonal micrometer readings give mean diameters 0.34 mm, 0.32 mm, and 0.33 mm (uncertainty $\pm 0.01$ mm). The gradient of the $F$ against $e$ graph has percentage uncertainty 1.6%. Calculate the total percentage uncertainty in the Young modulus $E$.
items.workedSolution: Mean diameter $d = 0.33$ mm gives $A = \pi d^2/4 = 8.55 × 10⁻⁸ m²$. $E = L \times \mathrm{grad} / A = 210 GPa$. Percentage uncertainty $\%\Delta E = \%\Delta L + 2\%\Delta d + \%\Delta\mathrm{grad} = 0.0769 + 2(3.03) + 1.6 = 7.74%$.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly evaluates pctUncE $= 7.74%$.

items.stem: A spinning orbital probe with extended telemetry booms has moment of inertia 32.0 kg m² and spins at 1.80 rad s⁻¹ with zero external torque. Internal actuators draw the booms inward, reducing the moment of inertia to 12.0 kg m².
items.workedSolution: (a) $\omega_2 = 4.80 rad s⁻¹$. (b) Work done $= \frac{1}{2}I_2\omega_2^2 - \frac{1}{2}I_1\omega_1^2 = 86.4 J$. (c) Internal radial forces do positive work pulling masses inward so rotational kinetic energy increases.

markScheme.criterion: Applies $I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$.
Obtains $\omega_2 = 4.80 rad s⁻¹$.
Calculates initial rotational KE $\frac{1}{2}I_1\omega_1^2$.
Calculates final rotational KE $\frac{1}{2}I_2\omega_2^2$ and finds difference.
Obtains internal work $= 86.4 J$.
Explains that radial actuator forces produce zero torque about the spin axis.
States that internal radial forces do positive work pulling the pods inward.

Calculate the work done by the internal winches in retracting the booms.

parts.expectedAnswer: Internal radial forces do positive work pulling masses inward so rotational kinetic energy increases.

Because the winches pull the pods inward against their outward tendency, internal radial forces do positive work increasing kinetic energy.

items.stem: Descending a rough warehouse ramp of length 10 m and vertical drop 2.5 m at a steady speed of 2.5 m s⁻¹, a heavy logistics crate has weight 450 N. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 450 × (2.5/10) = 113 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 281 W. Target = 113 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 113 N (B).

items.stem: In a light-string pendulum, a physics lecture bob of mass 0.5 kg hangs on a 1.8 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a stationary putty sphere of mass 0.5 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a physics lecture bob strikes a stationary putty sphere?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.94 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 14.7 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.97 m s⁻¹. Target = 14.7 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 14.7 N (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows the rotor of a dynamometer inertia brake rotor. Its central hub has moment of inertia 2.40 kg m² and carries 4 rim masses of 2.50 kg each at radius 0.480 m. During a test run lasting 9.00 s, the rotational speed changes uniformly from 16.0 rev s⁻¹ to 4.00 rev s⁻¹ while a constant bearing friction torque of 3.20 N m opposes rotation.
items.workedSolution: (a) $I = 4.70 kg m²$. (b) $|\alpha| = \frac{2\pi|f_2 - f_1|}{t} = 8.38 rad s⁻²$. (c) Applied torque $T_{\mathrm{app}} = 36.2 N m$. (d) Peak power $P_{\max} = T_{\mathrm{app}}\omega_{\max} = 3.64e+3 W$.

markScheme.criterion: Uses $I = I_{\mathrm{hub}} + \sum m r^2$ with squared radius.
Obtains $I = 4.70 kg m²$.
Converts $\text{rev s}^{-1}$ to $\text{rad s}^{-1}$ via $2\pi$ and divides change by $t$.
Obtains $|\alpha| = 8.38 rad s⁻²$.
Combines $I|\alpha|$ with bearing friction torque in the correct sense.
Obtains applied torque $= 36.2 N m$.
Applies $P = T\omega$ at the highest angular speed.
Obtains maximum power $= 3.64e+3 W$.

items.stem: Released from rest at the top of a straight steel loading chute of length 10 m inclined at 32° to the horizontal, an instrumented cargo crate of mass 6.5 kg reaches the bottom with speed 6.22 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the coefficient of dynamic friction μ_d between an instrumented cargo crate and a straight steel loading chute?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 32° = 338 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(6.5)(6.22)² = 126 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 212 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 32°)L, μ = 0.392. Target = 0.392.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 32° accurately to obtain 0.392 (D).

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a cantilevered boat-deck access hatch of length L = 2 m and mass 20 kg is smoothly hinged at O to a vertical wall and held horizontally in static equilibrium. Because of an internal reinforcing frame, its centre of gravity G lies 0.84 m from hinge O. A single steel cable attached to the outer edge pulls upward and toward the wall at an angle of 36° to the vertical (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). At what angle above the horizontal does the resultant reaction force R from hinge O act on the door?
items.workedSolution: Moments about O: T cos 36° × 2 = 20 × 9.81 × 0.84 ⇒ T = 101.9 N. Horizontal balance: R_x = T sin 36° = 59.87 N. Vertical balance: R_y = 20 × 9.81 − T cos 36° = 113.8 N. Resultant R = √(R_x² + R_y²) = 128.6 N ≈ 129 N, at angle α = tan⁻¹(R_y / R_x) = 62.25° ≈ 62.3° above the horizontal.

markScheme.criterion: Correct verified value = 62.3°.

items.stem: Dropped from rest at the anchor in a drop-test tower, an instrumented drop sphere of mass 2 kg falls freely 4 m until an elastic bungee tether becomes taut at A, then stretches the cord by 1.4 m over 0.18 s to come momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the mean upward force exerted by an elastic bungee tether between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 4) = 8.86 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.18 + 2(9.81) = 118 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 118 N (A).

items.stem: In a vertical-plane spinner, a gyroscope test mass of mass 3 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 2 m on a light radial tether, which snaps if tension exceeds 106 N. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed a gyroscope test mass can have at the bottom without breaking a light radial tether?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((106/3) − 9.81) × 2] = 7.14 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 7.14 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: B

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: In a cliff-sim drop frame, a mountaineering test mass of mass 8 kg is released from rest at the upper support of a dynamic climbing rope, which has natural unstretched length 4 m and obeys Hooke's law when taut. The cord first becomes taut at A and reaches maximum extension 0.85 m at lowest point B after an arrest interval of 0.28 s. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses free-fall relation v_A = √(2gL).
Obtains 8.86 m s⁻¹.
Equates mg(L + x) = ½kx² over the complete vertical drop.
Obtains 1.05 × 10³ N m⁻¹.
Evaluates a_B = (kx − mg) / m.
Obtains 102 m s⁻².

items.stem: The horizontal boom of a dockside container jib crane has total length L = 23 m and mass 1000 kg, supported on a vertical mast pivot P located 6 m from the rear end A. A concrete counterweight of mass 2800 kg sits 4.2 m to the left of P (1.8 m from A). The centre of gravity G of the boom itself lies 4.5 m to the right of P (10.5 m from A), and the hoist hook hangs 14.5 m to the right of P (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum safe load mass that can be suspended from the hook for rotational equilibrium about P?
items.workedSolution: Anticlockwise counterweight moment about P: M_cw = 2800 × 9.81 × 4.2 = 1.154 × 10⁵ N m. Clockwise boom moment: M_boom = 1000 × 9.81 × 4.5 = 4.415 × 10⁴ N m. Remaining clockwise moment available for load: W_max × 14.5 = 7.122 × 10⁴ N m ⇒ W_max = 4912 N ≈ 4.91e+3 N, m_max = W_max / 9.81 = 500.7 kg ≈ 501 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Correct maximum safe load mass = 501 kg.

items.stem: Along a level cleanroom linear rail, carrier X of mass 1.2 kg travels to the right at 9 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary carrier Y of mass 0.8 kg. Immediately after impact, carrier Y moves to the right at 8.48 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies m_X u_X = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y.
Obtains 3.35 m s⁻¹.
Sums ½m_X v_X² + ½m_Y v_Y².
Obtains 35.5 J.
Subtracts K_f from K_i = ½m_X u_X².
Obtains 13.1 J.

items.stem: Released from rest at the top of a textured service ramp of length 7.5 m inclined at 34° to the horizontal, a battery transport case of mass 13.5 kg reaches the bottom with speed 5.44 m s⁻¹ against a constant friction force. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the magnitude of the constant friction force opposing its motion?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 34° − ½mv² = 356 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 7.5 = 47.4 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.85 m s⁻¹. Target = 47.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 47.4 N (A).

items.stem: Along a precision gas-bearing trough, rider X of mass 0.8 kg moves to the right at 6 m s⁻¹ and strikes stationary rider Y of mass 2.9 kg. Immediately after the collision, rider Y moves to the right at 2.17 m s⁻¹. Take rightward as positive.

markScheme.criterion: Applies signed momentum conservation m_X u_X = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y.
Obtains 1.87 m s⁻¹ to the left.
Adds positive scalar kinetic energies ½m_X v_X² + ½m_Y v_Y².
Obtains 8.22 J.
Evaluates K_i − K_f.
Obtains 6.18 J.

items.stem: In a circular motion demonstrator, a polymer-coated mass of mass 3.3 kg is attached to a light inextensible string of length 1.3 m and moves in a vertical circle, passing through the lowest point with speed 6.5 m s⁻¹. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_c = mv² / r.
Obtains 107 N.
Applies T − mg = F_c => T = F_c + mg.
Obtains 140 N.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant centripetal force on a polymer-coated mass at the lowest point.
Hence calculate the tension in a light inextensible string at the lowest point.

items.stem: Projected from a calibrated ground launcher at 45 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 33° above a flat proving ground, an acoustic ranging dart follows a parabolic arc. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 33° = 37.7 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 33°)² / (2g) = 30.6 m. Target = 37.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 33° at apex to obtain 37.7 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a shipyard maintenance gangway plank AB of total length L = 4.8 m and mass 19 kg is uniform, with its centre of gravity G at its midpoint (2.4 m from end A). The beam rests horizontally in equilibrium on a sharp pivot P positioned 1.34 m from end A when a counterbalance block of unknown mass is placed 0.34 m from end A (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the upward reaction force R exerted by pivot P on the balanced beam?
items.workedSolution: Take moments about pivot P. Lever arm of beam CG is d_G = 2.4 − 1.34 = 1.060 m. Lever arm of counterbalance is d_load = 1.34 − 0.34 = 1.000 m. Balancing moments: m_load g d_load = m_beam g d_G ⇒ m_load = (19 × 1.060) / 1.000 = 20.14 kg ≈ 20.1 kg. Vertical equilibrium gives R = (m_beam + m_load)g = (19 + 20.14) × 9.81 = 384.0 N ≈ 384 N.

markScheme.criterion: Correct upward pivot reaction R = 384 N.

items.stem: On a smooth marshalling test track, wagon X of mass 3 kg moves right at 9 m s⁻¹ toward wagon Y of mass 4.2 kg approaching head-on to the left at 5.5 m s⁻¹ (initial arrow on Y omitted). Immediately after collision, wagon Y moves right at 4 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of wagon X immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (3)(9) + (4.2)(−5.5) = 3.90 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (3)v_X + (4.2)(4), v_X = -4.30 m s⁻¹, which is 4.30 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 3.90 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 4.30 m s⁻¹ to the left (B).

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a lakeside wooden viewing jetty plank of total length L = 4.8 m and mass 48 kg rests horizontally on two narrow supports A and B. Support A is positioned at its left end, and support B is 3.4 m to the right of A, leaving an unsupported right-hand overhang of 1.4 m. A technician of mass 60 kg initially stands 1.5 m from the left end of the plank (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the upward reaction force F₁ exerted by support A while the technician stands at the initial position?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about B: F₁ × 3.4 = (48 × 1.000 + 60 × 1.900) × 9.81 ⇒ F₁ = 467.4 N ≈ 467 N. At tipping (F₁ = 0): m_load × d_tip = m_beam × (x_B − x_G) ⇒ d_tip = (48 × 1.000) / 60 = 0.8000 m ≈ 0.800 m. At the very tip (overhang 1.4 m): m_end = (48 × 1.000) / 1.4 = 34.29 kg ≈ 34.3 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Correct solver-verified answer = 467 N.

items.stem: On calm water at launch level, a deck-level launcher launches a rescue line-throwing bob from ground level at speed 38 m s⁻¹ and angle 34° above the horizontal. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates u_y = u sin θ.
Obtains 21.2 m s⁻¹.
Applies T = 2u_y / g.
Obtains 4.33 s.
Multiplies u cos θ by flight time T.
Obtains 136 m.

Calculate the horizontal range of the trajectory.

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a rail-yard test locomotive of mass 1200 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-hung indicator sphere hangs at 26° to the vertical, later climbs a 14° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 45 m (static friction coefficient 0.5), and coasts from 21 m s⁻¹ against a 530 N resistive force toward the buffer platform. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a roof-hung indicator sphere deflects by 26°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 26° = ma and T cos 26° = mg => a = g tan 26° = 4.78 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.5 × 9.81 × 45) = 14.9 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1200)(21)² / 530 = 499 m. Target = 4.78 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 4.78 m s⁻² (C).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: On the skydiver's velocity–time graph, the curve flattens into a horizontal plateau at point Q. Which force condition explains this horizontal section?
items.workedSolution: At terminal velocity Q, upward drag equals downward weight so resultant force is zero and velocity is constant (Newton's first law). Therefore option C is correct: upward drag equals downward weight so resultant force is zero and velocity is constant.

markScheme.criterion: Select option C: upward drag equals downward weight so resultant force is zero and velocity is constant.

items.stem: A dressed limestone drainage channel of length L = 3.00 m rests horizontally on level ground (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). As shown in the figure, it has a semi-annular cross-section of outer diameter D = 25.0 cm and inner diameter d = 15.0 cm and average density ρ = 2480 kg m⁻³. The component is uniform along its length so its centre of gravity G lies at its midpoint. A compact construction crane rated at electrical input power 620 W and efficiency 82% is later attached to end B to stand the component vertically upright on end A.
items.workedSolution: (a) A = 0.01571 m², V = A L = 0.04712 m³, m = ρ V = 116.9 kg ≈ 117 kg. (b) W = 1146 N; taking moments about A gives F = W × (x_G / L) = 573.2 N ≈ 573 N. (c) Centre of gravity rises by Δh = 1.500 m, so ΔE_p = m g Δh = 1720 J ≈ 1.72e+3 J. (d) Useful power P_out = 0.82 × 620 = 508.4 W, so t = 1720 / 508.4 = 3.383 s ≈ 3.38 s. (e) density is uniform and negligible work is done against friction or giving kinetic energy to the beam.

markScheme.criterion: Computes semi-annular cross-section A = (π/8)(D² − d²) = 0.01571 m² with cm → m conversion.
Calculates V = A L = 0.04712 m³ and substitutes m = ρ V.
Shows 4 s.f. mass 116.9 kg rounding clearly to 117 kg.
Applies principle of moments about A: F × 3.00 = m g × 1.500.
Evaluates minimum lift force F = 573 N (4 s.f. 573.2 N).
Uses centre-of-gravity rise Δh = 1.500 m (not full length L) in ΔE_p = m g Δh.
Obtains work done = 1.72e+3 J (4 s.f. 1720 J).
Applies useful power P_out = η P_in = 508.4 W and t = ΔE_p / P_out.
Evaluates minimum hoist time = 3.38 s (4 s.f. 3.383 s).
States valid physical assumption: density is uniform and negligible work is done against friction or giving kinetic energy to the beam.

items.stem: A basalt roadside runnel section of length L = 2.60 m rests horizontally on level ground (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). As shown in the figure, it has a semi-annular cross-section of outer diameter D = 22.0 cm and inner diameter d = 12.0 cm and average density ρ = 2780 kg m⁻³. The component is uniform along its length so its centre of gravity G lies at its midpoint. A mobile crane hoist motor rated at electrical input power 580 W and efficiency 80% is later attached to end B to stand the component vertically upright on end A.
items.workedSolution: (a) A = 0.01335 m², V = A L = 0.03471 m³, m = ρ V = 96.51 kg ≈ 96.5 kg. (b) W = 946.7 N; taking moments about A gives F = W × (x_G / L) = 473.4 N ≈ 473 N. (c) Centre of gravity rises by Δh = 1.300 m, so ΔE_p = m g Δh = 1231 J ≈ 1.23e+3 J. (d) Useful power P_out = 0.80 × 580 = 464.0 W, so t = 1231 / 464.0 = 2.652 s ≈ 2.65 s. (e) electrical heating in the motor windings and friction in the hoist gears dissipate thermal energy to the surroundings.

markScheme.criterion: Calculates cross-section A = 0.01335 m², volume V = 0.03471 m³, and applies m = ρ V.
Shows 4 s.f. mass 96.51 kg confirming 96.5 kg.
Applies principle of moments about A: F × 2.60 = m g × 1.300.
Evaluates minimum lift force F = 473 N (4 s.f. 473.4 N).
Uses centre-of-gravity rise Δh = 1.300 m (not full length L) in ΔE_p = m g Δh.
Obtains work done = 1.23e+3 J (4 s.f. 1231 J).
Applies useful power P_out = η P_in = 464.0 W and t = ΔE_p / P_out.
Evaluates minimum hoist time = 2.65 s (4 s.f. 2.652 s).
Identifies electrical heating in motor windings and mechanical friction in hoist gears.
Links losses to thermal energy dissipated to the surroundings (electrical heating in the motor windings and friction in the hoist gears dissipate thermal energy to the surroundings).

items.stem: In Required Practical 3, a student drops a dense steel sphere through two light gates and plots $2h/t$ against $t$. The best-fit straight line has gradient 9.74 m s⁻² (with percentage uncertainty 2.1%) and vertical intercept 2.28 m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) $u = 2.28/2 = 1.14 m s⁻¹$. (b) $\Delta g = 0.205 m s⁻²$. (c) Percentage difference $= 0.714%$ (smaller than the 2.1% experimental uncertainty, so result is consistent with 9.81 m s⁻²). (d) use a plumb line to align the metre ruler vertically and plot two h over t against t so the gradient equals gravitational field strength independently of initial speed.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies vertical intercept equals $2u$.
Initial speed $u = 1.14 m s⁻¹$.
Multiplies measured $g$ by fractional uncertainty.
Absolute uncertainty $\Delta g = 0.205 m s⁻²$.
Computes $|g_{\mathrm{meas}} - 9.81|/9.81 \times 100\%$.
Percentage difference $= 0.714%$.
Uses a plumb line / set square against bench to ensure ruler is strictly vertical.
Shows $2h/t = gt + 2u$ keeps gradient equal to $g$ regardless of initial speed $u$.

2h/t = gt + 2u separates unknown u into the vertical intercept while gradient stays g.

items.stem: In the electromagnet-and-trapdoor arrangement of Required Practical 3, plotting drop height $h$ against $t^2$ produces a straight line of gradient 4.84 m s⁻². In an individual drop from $h = 1.45$ m, the digital timer records 0.5547 s because residual magnetism delays release by 11 ms.
items.workedSolution: (a) $g = 2 \times 4.84 = 9.68 m s⁻²$. (b) Percentage difference $= 1.33%$. (c) Single drop gives $g = 9.42 m s⁻²$. (d) residual magnetism in the electromagnet delays sphere release making the recorded fall time too large and producing a systematic underestimate of g.

markScheme.criterion: Uses $g = 2 \times \mathrm{gradient}$.
Measured $g = 9.68 m s⁻²$.
Divides absolute discrepancy by accepted $9.81$ m s⁻².
Percentage difference $= 1.33%$.
Substitutes into $g = 2h/t^2$.
Apparent $g = 9.42 m s⁻²$.
Residual magnetism delays release so recorded $t$ is systematically too large.
Suggests reducing electromagnet current / inserting paper spacer / using two light gates.

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a greenhouse irrigation-manifold support bar of total length L = 2.8 m and mass 34 kg hangs horizontally in equilibrium from two light ceiling wires attached at A and B (1.9 m apart), with wire An inclined at 50° above the horizontal bar. Its centre of gravity G lies 1.25 m to the right of attachment A and 0.65 m to the left of attachment B (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Moments about B yield T₁ = 149.0 N ≈ 149 N. (b) Force balance gives T₂ = 239.4 N ≈ 239 N. (c) wire B carries the greater tension because the centre of gravity is closer to wire B.

markScheme.criterion: Applies moment balance about attachment B.
Combines vertical and horizontal equilibrium components for wire B.
Identifies the wire closer to G as carrying greater tension.
Justifies using equal opposite moments about G with shorter lever arm.

Show that the wire with the shorter perpendicular distance to G must exert the larger tension to balance moments.

items.workedSolution: (a) Static equilibrium requires zero resultant force and zero resultant moment about any point. (b) Torque of the couple is T = F d_perp = 19.05 N m ≈ 19.1 N m (note N m, not J).

Zero resultant moment about any point.
Applies T = F d_perp using perpendicular separation.

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a museum gallery wall-mounted support bar is a uniform horizontal rod of length L = 1.6 m and mass 11 kg smoothly hinged to a vertical wall at O. A rectangular sign of mass 6.5 kg hangs so that its centre of gravity acts 1.3 m from O. A taut support wire joins the outer end of the rod to the wall at an angle of 44° above the horizontal rod (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the vertical upward component of force exerted on the rod by hinge O?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about hinge O: T sin 44° × 1.6 = (11 × 0.8 + 6.5 × 1.3) × 9.81 = 169.2 N m. Hence T sin 44° = 105.8 N and T = 152.3 N ≈ 152 N. Horizontal balance: R_x = T cos 44° = 109.5 N ≈ 110 N. Vertical balance: R_y = (11 + 6.5) × 9.81 − 105.8 = 65.91 N ≈ 65.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Correct verified value = 65.9 N.

items.stem: In Searle's Young modulus investigation (RP4) on a hard-drawn steel wire of unstretched length $(2.40 \pm 0.002)$ m, micrometer diameter measurements at three orthogonal positions average to 0.42 mm, 0.44 mm, and 0.43 mm (each $\pm 0.01$ mm). Plotting load $F$ against extension $e$ yields a straight line through the origin of gradient 12.1 N mm⁻¹ ($\pm 2.0\%$).
items.workedSolution: (a) $A = \pi d^2/4 = 1.45 × 10⁻⁷ m²$. (b) $E = L(\mathrm{grad})/A = 200 GPa$. (c) $\%\Delta E = 6.73%$. (d) an identical reference wire compensates both ceiling sag and thermal expansion while orthogonal micrometer diameter measurements reduce cross sectional area uncertainty.

markScheme.criterion: Averages three diameters and converts mm to m in $A = \pi d^2/4$.
Cross-sectional area $A = 1.45 × 10⁻⁷ m²$.
Converts gradient to N m⁻¹ and substitutes into $E = (L/A)\,\mathrm{grad}$.
Young modulus $E = 200 GPa$.
Combines $\%\Delta L + 2\%\Delta d + \%\Delta\mathrm{grad}$.
Percentage uncertainty in $E = 6.73%$.
Identical reference wire compensates both support sag and temperature expansion.
Orthogonal micrometer readings at >= 3 positions detect non-uniformity/oval cross-section.

items.stem: Two coaxial clutch discs rotate in opposite senses on a frictionless shaft: Disc 1 has $I_1 = 1.20\text{ kg m}^2$ at $+40.0\text{ rad s}^{-1}$ and Disc 2 has $I_2 = 1.80\text{ kg m}^2$ at $-10.0\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. When engaged together they reach a common angular speed. How much rotational kinetic energy is dissipated as heat?
items.workedSolution: Initial angular momentum $L = 1.20(40.0) + 1.80(-10.0) = 30.0\text{ N m s}$, giving $\omega_{\mathrm{f}} = \frac{30.0}{3.00} = 10.0\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. Initial KE $= \frac{1}{2}(1.20)(40^2) + \frac{1}{2}(1.80)(10^2) = 1050\text{ J}$; final KE $= \frac{1}{2}(3.00)(10^2) = 150\text{ J}$. Energy dissipated $= 900 J$.

markScheme.criterion: Thermal energy dissipated equals 900 J.

items.stem: A single-cylinder four-stroke diesel generator requires a heavy steel flywheel on its crankshaft, whereas an electric induction motor of the same mean power output does not. The turning-moment graph illustrates the cyclic torque delivered by the diesel engine against crankshaft angle.
items.workedSolution: A four-stroke engine produces driving torque on only one of its four strokes while an electric motor gives steady torque. On the turning-moment diagram, the flywheel absorbs excess energy when engine torque exceeds mean load and releases energy during zero-torque strokes. Since $\Delta E = \frac{1}{2}I(\omega_{\max}^2 - \omega_{\min}^2) = I\bar{\omega}\Delta\omega$, a large moment of inertia $I$ keeps speed fluctuation $\Delta\omega$ small, balanced against slower deliberate acceleration.

markScheme.criterion: States that a four-stroke engine produces driving torque during only one stroke in four whereas an electric motor provides nearly steady torque.
Notes that torque falls to zero or negative during induction, compression, and exhaust strokes.
Explains from the graph that excess energy above the mean-load line accelerates the flywheel and increases its rotational kinetic energy.
Explains that when engine torque is below the mean load, the flywheel decelerates and supplies energy to keep the shaft turning through compression.
Applies $\Delta E = \frac{1}{2}I(\omega_{\max}^2 - \omega_{\min}^2)$ to show that larger moment of inertia $I$ gives a smaller speed fluctuation $\Delta\omega$.
Identifies a valid practical design trade-off such as slower deliberate acceleration or extra mass/bearing load from a very large flywheel.

parts.prompt: Explain why the diesel engine needs a flywheel to maintain steady speed under constant load while the electric motor does not, referencing the turning-moment diagram and the role of moment of inertia in limiting speed fluctuations.
parts.expectedAnswer: A four-stroke diesel cylinder delivers positive driving torque during only one of its four strokes, with negative or near-zero torque during induction, compression, and exhaust, whereas an electric motor supplies nearly continuous torque. On the turning-moment diagram, the flywheel absorbs excess energy when engine torque exceeds mean load and releases energy during zero-torque strokes so the crankshaft continues turning smoothly through compression. Because cyclic energy exchange equals half times moment of inertia times the difference in squared angular speeds, increasing the moment of inertia reduces the angular speed fluctuation for a given energy pulse, although excessive inertia slows deliberate throttle response.
workingSteps: L1: Contrast the single power stroke per two revolutions of a four-stroke engine with the nearly steady torque of an electric motor.
L1: Identify that engine torque falls below the mean load (and goes negative during compression) for most of the cycle.
L2: Link positive shaded areas above the mean-load line to excess work stored as rotational kinetic energy while the flywheel accelerates.
L2: Link regions below the mean-load line to kinetic energy released by the flywheel to drive the load and compress gas.
L3: Use $\Delta E = \frac{1}{2}I(\omega_{\max}^2 - \omega_{\min}^2) = I\omega_{\mathrm{mean}}\Delta\omega$ to explain why large $I$ keeps $\Delta\omega$ small.
L3: Note the engineering trade-off that a larger moment of inertia also reduces responsiveness when changing speed deliberately.

items.stem: Released from rest from a horizontal string position of length 1.7 m in a fracture-toughness pendulum, a hardened striker ball (2.4 kg) strikes and sticks to stationary a soft polymer target (1.92 kg) at the bottom of its arc. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. How much mechanical energy is dissipated during the sticking collision?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 5.77 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 3.21 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.525 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 17.8 J. Target = 17.8 J.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 17.8 J (B).

items.stem: A test disc of hub inertia 2.10 kg m² carrying 4 masses of 2.00 kg at radius 0.45 m slows uniformly from 12.0 rev s⁻¹ to 4.0 rev s⁻¹ in 6.0 s. Bearing friction contributes a constant retarding torque of 3.50 N m, and a brake pad presses tangentially at radius 0.25 m. What tangential friction force does the brake pad exert?
items.workedSolution: $I = 2.10 + 4(2.00)(0.45)^2 = 3.72\text{ kg m}^2$. Deceleration $|\alpha| = \frac{2\pi(12.0 - 4.0)}{6.0} = 8.38\text{ rad s}^{-2}$. Net retarding torque $|T_{\mathrm{net}}| = I|\alpha| = 31.2\text{ N m}$. Brake torque $T_{\mathrm{brake}} = 31.2 - 3.50 = 27.7\text{ N m}$, so $F = \frac{T_{\mathrm{brake}}}{r} = \frac{27.7}{0.25} = 111 N$.

markScheme.criterion: Brake pad tangential force equals 111 N.

items.stem: As shown in the figure, an industrial kiln hinged heat-shield door of length L = 1.8 m and mass 12 kg is smoothly hinged at O to a vertical wall and held horizontally in static equilibrium. Because of an internal reinforcing frame, its centre of gravity G lies 0.72 m from hinge O. A single steel cable attached to the outer edge pulls upward and toward the wall at an angle of 30° to the vertical (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 54.37 N ≈ 54.4 N. (b) the angled wire exerts a horizontal component pulling toward the wall so the hinge must provide an equal horizontal force away from the wall for translational equilibrium. (c)(i) R_x = 27.19 N, R_y = 70.63 N, so R = 75.68 N ≈ 75.7 N. (c)(ii) α = tan⁻¹(R_y / R_x) = 68.95° ≈ 68.9° above the horizontal.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Στ = 0 about O using T cos(angle to vertical) × L = m g x_G.
Obtains T = 54.37 N (54.4 N) matching 54 N.
Identifies horizontal component of angled cable tension directed toward the wall.
States hinge must exert an equal opposite horizontal force away from the wall for ΣF_x = 0.
Computes R_x = 27.19 N and R_y = 70.63 N and applies Pythagoras.
Resultant hinge reaction magnitude R = 75.7 N.
Uses tan α = R_y / R_x with both hinge components.
Direction α = 68.9° above the horizontal.

items.stem: Released from rest at the anchor of an elastic recovery cord (natural length 1.8 m) in a vertical test bay, an aerospace drop canister of mass 9 kg falls freely to point A where the cord becomes taut, then stretches the cord by 1.1 m over 0.21 s before reaching instantaneous rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates v_A = √(2gL).
Obtains 5.94 m s⁻¹.
Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = m v_A, including weight mg.
Mean resultant upward force = (9 × 5.94) / 0.21 = 255 N.
Obtains 343 N.
Uses mg(L + x) = ½kx² and T_B = kx.
Obtains 465 N.

items.stem: Released from rest at the support in a fall-arrest gantry, a rescue arrest dummy (8.5 kg) falls freely through the 1.8 m natural length of a braided dynamic lanyard to point A and then extends the Hookean cord by 1.35 m during 0.32 s to instantaneous rest at B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the peak tension in a braided dynamic lanyard at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 1.8 + 1.35 = 3.15 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 288 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 389 N. Target = 389 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (1.8 + 1.35) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 389 N (B).

items.stem: The horizontal boom of a cargo-terminal balanced derrick boom has total length L = 25 m and mass 550 kg, supported on a vertical mast pivot P located 4.5 m from the rear end A. A concrete counterweight of mass 3000 kg sits 2.7 m to the left of P (1.8 m from A). The centre of gravity G of the boom itself lies 3 m to the right of P (7.5 m from A), and the hoist hook hangs 19.5 m to the right of P (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) M_cw = 7.946 × 10⁴ N m ≈ 7.95 × 10⁴ N m. (b) Equating clockwise and anticlockwise moments about P gives m_max = 330.8 kg ≈ 331 kg. (c) Vertical force balance yields R = 3.807 × 10⁴ N ≈ 3.81 × 10⁴ N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses M = m g d with counterweight mass and lever arm from P.
Counterweight moment = 7.95 × 10⁴ N m.
Subtracts boom self-weight moment from counterweight moment and divides by g × load lever arm.
Maximum safe load mass = 331 kg.
Applies vertical force balance summing counterweight, boom, and load weights.
Upward mast reaction R = 3.81 × 10⁴ N.

parts.prompt: Calculate the anticlockwise moment exerted by the concrete counterweight about pivot P.
workingSteps: Moment M_cw = W_cw × 2.7 = 7.946 × 10⁴ N m ≈ 7.95 × 10⁴ N m.

parts.prompt: Taking into account the weight of the boom, determine the maximum load mass that can be lifted at the hoist hook so the net moment about P is zero.
workingSteps: Clockwise moment of boom = 550 × 9.81 × 3 = 1.619 × 10⁴ N m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total upward reaction force exerted by the vertical mast pivot P when this maximum load is suspended in equilibrium.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium: R = (m_cw + m_boom + m_max) g.

items.stem: Travelling at 12 m s⁻¹ to the right along a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, shuttle X (3.6 kg) strikes stationary shuttle Y (2.8 kg), sending shuttle Y rightward at 10.08 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of shuttle X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (3.6)(12) = (3.6)v_X + (2.8)(10.08), giving v_X = 4.16 m s⁻¹. K_i = 259 J and K_f = 173 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 85.8 J. Target = 4.16 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 4.16 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Released from rest at the top of a roughened hardwood slope of length 4.5 m inclined at 26° to the horizontal, a brass counterweight slider of mass 15 kg slides against a constant friction force and reaches the bottom at 3.11 m s⁻¹. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates mgL sin θ − ½mv².
Obtains 217 J.
Divides dissipated energy from (a) by ramp length L.
Obtains 48.3 N.
Recognizes unchanged acceleration and applies v² ∝ s => v_new = v / √2.
Obtains 2.20 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Moving rightward at 9 m s⁻¹ on a level cleanroom linear rail, carrier X (2 kg) collides head-on with stationary carrier Y (6.8 kg); immediately afterward carrier Y travels right at 3.87 m s⁻¹ and carrier X rebounds backward. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (2)(9) = (2)v_X + (6.8)(3.87) gives v_X = -4.16 m s⁻¹ (4.16 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(2)(4.16)² + ½(6.8)(3.87)² = 68.2 J. Energy lost = 81.0 J − K_f = 12.8 J. Target = 68.2 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 4.16 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 68.2 J (D).

items.stem: Whirled on a taut nylon cord of length 0.7 m in a vertical whirl apparatus, a brass pendulum mass (2.7 kg) has speed 6 m s⁻¹ at the bottom of its vertical circular path. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the tension in a taut nylon cord at this instant.
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 2.7 × 6² / 0.7 = 139 N, so T = 139 + 2.7 × 9.8 = 165 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 165 N (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: Launched from a spring-loaded catapult across a level arena floor, a robotics arena sphere has an initial speed of 21 m s⁻¹ at 24° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) v_apex = 21 × cos 24°. Answer: 19.2 m s⁻¹. (b) u_y = 21 × sin 24° = 8.54 m s⁻¹. h_max = u_y² / (2 × 9.8). Answer: 3.72 m. (c) T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 1.74 s. R = 19.2 × T. Answer: 33.4 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes v_y = 0 at apex so v_apex = u cos θ.
Obtains 19.2 m s⁻¹.
Applies h_max = (u sin θ)² / (2g).
Obtains 3.72 m.
Evaluates R = u_x × (2u_y / g).
Obtains 33.4 m.

items.stem: In a workshop statics test, a rowing-club boathouse oar-rack beam AB of length L = 4.8 m and mass 8 kg has its centre of gravity G at 2.78 m from end A. It is balanced horizontally on a knife-edge pivot P located 1.34 m from end A by placing a 14 kg calibration block to the left of P (use g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) The moment of a force is the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action. (b) Moment balance about P gives d = 0.8229 m left of P, so distance from end B is 4.283 m ≈ 4.28 m.

markScheme.criterion: Force multiplied by distance from pivot.
Perpendicular distance to the line of action.
Correct moment balance about P yielding lever arm d = 0.8229 m.
Converts cleanly to distance from end B = 4.28 m.

parts.prompt: State the definition of the moment of a force about a point.
parts.expectedAnswer: It is the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action.
workingSteps: State force multiplied by distance from the pivot.
Include the requirement that the distance is perpendicular to the line of action of the force.

parts.prompt: Determine the distance from end B at which the calibration block must be placed so that the beam balances horizontally.
workingSteps: Clockwise moment of beam weight about P = 8 × 9.81 × 1.440.
Equate with anticlockwise moment of block: d = (8 × 1.440) / 14 = 0.8229 m to the left of P.

items.stem: On a level low-friction dynamics rail, cart X of mass 3.5 kg moves to the right at 12 m s⁻¹ and collides head-on with cart Y of mass 3.6 kg moving to the left at 3 m s⁻¹ (arrow on Y not shown). Immediately after impact, cart Y moves to the right at 2 m s⁻¹. Take motion to the right as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 3.5 × 12 + 3.6 × (−3) = 31.2 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 31.2 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (31.2 − 3.6 × 2) / 3.5 = 6.86 m s⁻¹. Answer: 6.86 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m_X u_X − m_Y |u_Y| with correct signs.
Obtains 31.2 kg m s⁻¹ to the right.
Solves p_before = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y for v_X.
Obtains 6.86 m s⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a theatre stage apron extension beam of total length L = 5 m and mass 36 kg rests horizontally on two narrow supports A and B. Support A is positioned 0.6 m from its left end, and support B is 2.8 m to the right of A, leaving an unsupported right-hand overhang of 1.6 m. A technician of mass 74 kg initially stands 1.3 m from the left end of the plank (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Moments about B give F₁ = 658.0 N ≈ 658 N. (b) Vertical equilibrium gives F₂ = 421.1 N ≈ 421 N. (c) the reaction force at support A decreases and the reaction force at support B increases. (d) Setting F₁ = 0 about B yields d_tip = 0.4378 m ≈ 0.438 m.

markScheme.criterion: Takes moments about B summing plank and technician anticlockwise moments.
Support A reaction F₁ = 658 N.
Support B reaction F₂ = 421 N via vertical force balance.
States that the reaction force at support A decreases and the reaction force at support B increases.
Sets F₁ = 0 and equates clockwise overhang moment to restoring plank moment about B.
Tipping distance past B = 0.438 m.

parts.prompt: By taking moments about support B, calculate the upward reaction force F₁ at support A while the technician is at the initial position.
workingSteps: Clockwise moment of F₁ about B = F₁ × 2.8.

parts.prompt: Deduce the upward reaction force F₂ at support B.
State qualitatively how the reaction forces at supports A and B change as the technician walks slowly toward the right-hand overhang.
parts.expectedAnswer: As the technician moves toward the overhang, the reaction force at support A decreases and the reaction force at support B increases.
workingSteps: Explain that shifting weight toward support B reduces the anticlockwise moment about B so support A carries less load while support B carries more.

parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum distance past support B that the technician can walk onto the overhang before the plank begins to tip.
workingSteps: At the tipping limit, F₁ = 0; take moments about B: 74 g d_tip = 36 g (0.9000).

items.stem: Fired from a spring-loaded catapult at 34 m s⁻¹ and 26° above the horizontal, a robotics arena sphere lands back on a level arena floor. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the total time of flight before returning to a level arena floor?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 34 sin 26° = 14.9 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 34 cos 26° = 30.6 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 3.04 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 93.0 m. Target = 3.04 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 3.04 s (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: During proving-ground tests, an electric quarry haulage rig of mass 1400 kg accelerates along a level straight so a suspended brass bob deflects by 30° from the vertical, climbs a straight 12° incline at constant speed, negotiates a flat semicircular curve of radius 85 m (coefficient of static friction 0.8), and finally coasts along the semicircle from 18 m s⁻¹ against a constant 530 N resistance toward the weighbridge. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance.

markScheme.criterion: Uses T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg => a = g tan θ.
Obtains 5.66 m s⁻².
Applies μ_s mg = m v_max² / R.
Obtains 25.8 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts resistive work F_res(πR) from initial kinetic energy ½mu².
Obtains 11.0 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: By resolving forces on a suspended brass bob, calculate the horizontal acceleration when the string deflects by 30°.
Calculate the maximum speed on the flat semicircular road without sliding.
Calculate the speed with which an electric quarry haulage rig reaches the weighbridge at the end of the semicircular coast.

items.stem: A skydiver descends at constant terminal velocity as shown in the force diagram.
items.workedSolution: (a) equal magnitude opposite direction same type of force acting on two different bodies; weight and drag act on the same body and are different force types. (b) gravitational pull of the skydiver upward on the Earth.

markScheme.criterion: Weight and drag both act on the same body (skydiver), whereas N3L pairs act on two different bodies.
Weight (gravitational) and drag (contact/electromagnetic) are different types of force.
Gravitational pull exerted by the skydiver on the Earth.
Equal in magnitude and directed upwards (towards the skydiver).

parts.prompt: Explain why the skydiver's downward weight and upward air drag are NOT a Newton's third law pair.
parts.expectedAnswer: Weight and drag act on the same object and are different types of force, whereas a Newton's third law pair requires equal magnitude opposite direction same type of force acting on two different bodies.
workingSteps: Contrast same-body equilibrium (N1L) with two-body same-type N3L interaction.

parts.prompt: State the exact Newton's third law partner force to the skydiver's weight.
parts.expectedAnswer: The partner force is the gravitational pull of the skydiver upward on the Earth of equal magnitude.
workingSteps: Identify gravitational force exerted by the skydiver upward on the Earth.

items.stem: A polymer-concrete cable duct of length L = 2.50 m rests horizontally on level ground (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). As shown in the figure, it has a semi-annular cross-section of outer diameter D = 26.0 cm and inner diameter d = 16.0 cm and average density ρ = 2150 kg m⁻³. The component is uniform along its length so its centre of gravity G lies at its midpoint. A geared electric hoist rated at electrical input power 480 W and efficiency 76% is later attached to end B to stand the component vertically upright on end A.
items.workedSolution: (a) A = 0.01649 m², V = A L = 0.04123 m³, m = ρ V = 88.65 kg ≈ 88.7 kg. (b) W = 869.7 N; taking moments about A gives F = W × (x_G / L) = 434.8 N ≈ 435 N. (c) Centre of gravity rises by Δh = 1.250 m, so ΔE_p = m g Δh = 1087 J ≈ 1.09e+3 J. (d) Useful power P_out = 0.76 × 480 = 364.8 W, so t = 1087 / 364.8 = 2.980 s ≈ 2.98 s. (e) density is uniform and negligible work is done against friction or giving kinetic energy to the beam.

markScheme.criterion: Computes semi-annular cross-section A = (π/8)(D² − d²) = 0.01649 m² with cm → m conversion.
Calculates V = A L = 0.04123 m³ and substitutes m = ρ V.
Shows 4 s.f. mass 88.65 kg rounding clearly to 88.7 kg.
Applies principle of moments about A: F × 2.50 = m g × 1.250.
Evaluates minimum lift force F = 435 N (4 s.f. 434.8 N).
Uses centre-of-gravity rise Δh = 1.250 m (not full length L) in ΔE_p = m g Δh.
Obtains work done = 1.09e+3 J (4 s.f. 1087 J).
Applies useful power P_out = η P_in = 364.8 W and t = ΔE_p / P_out.
Evaluates minimum hoist time = 2.98 s (4 s.f. 2.980 s).
States valid physical assumption: density is uniform and negligible work is done against friction or giving kinetic energy to the beam.

items.stem: A non-uniform hardwood bridge sleeper of length L = 2.60 m rests horizontally on level ground (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). As shown in the figure, it has a rectangular cross-section of width w = 26.0 cm and thickness h = 16.0 cm and average density ρ = 1150 kg m⁻³. Internal reinforcement makes the component non-uniform so its centre of gravity G lies at distance x = 1.09 m from end A (as shown). A trackside battery winch rated at electrical input power 340 W and efficiency 74% is later attached to end B to stand the component vertically upright on end A.
items.workedSolution: (a) A = 0.04160 m², V = A L = 0.1082 m³, m = ρ V = 124.4 kg ≈ 124 kg. (b) W = 1220 N; taking moments about A gives F = W × (x_G / L) = 512.5 N ≈ 512 N. (c) Centre of gravity rises by Δh = 1.092 m, so ΔE_p = m g Δh = 1332 J ≈ 1.33e+3 J. (d) Useful power P_out = 0.74 × 340 = 251.6 W, so t = 1332 / 251.6 = 5.296 s ≈ 5.30 s. (e) electrical heating in the motor windings and friction in the hoist gears dissipate thermal energy to the surroundings.

Shows 4 s.f. mass 124.4 kg confirming 124 kg.
Applies principle of moments about A: F × 2.60 = m g × 1.092.
Evaluates minimum lift force F = 512 N (4 s.f. 512.5 N).
Uses centre-of-gravity rise Δh = 1.092 m (not full length L) in ΔE_p = m g Δh.
Obtains work done = 1.33e+3 J (4 s.f. 1332 J).
Applies useful power P_out = η P_in = 251.6 W and t = ΔE_p / P_out.
Evaluates minimum hoist time = 5.30 s (4 s.f. 5.296 s).
Identifies electrical heating in motor windings and mechanical friction in hoist gears.
Links losses to thermal energy dissipated to the surroundings (electrical heating in the motor windings and friction in the hoist gears dissipate thermal energy to the surroundings).

items.stem: In Required Practical 3 using two light gates, a student plots $2h/t$ against $t$ and finds a straight line of gradient 9.92 m s⁻² and vertical intercept 3.16 m s⁻¹. Calculate the percentage difference between this measured value of $g$ and the accepted value $9.81$ m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: From $h = ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^2$, rearranging gives $2h/t = gt + 2u$. Thus $g = 9.92$ m s⁻², $u = 3.16 / 2 = 1.58 m s⁻¹$, and percentage difference $= |9.92 - 9.81|/9.81 \times 100\% = 1.12%$.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly evaluates pctDiffG $= 1.12%$.

items.stem: Why does Required Practical 3 specify a small, dense steel sphere rather than a large hollow plastic ball, and what systematic effect mimics air drag in the electromagnet setup?
items.workedSolution: RP3 evaluation: High weight-to-drag ratio keeps air resistance negligible; alongside air drag, residual magnetism in the electromagnet delays sphere release making the recorded fall time too large and producing a systematic underestimate of g.

markScheme.criterion: High weight-to-drag ratio keeps air resistance negligible; alongside air drag, residual magnetism in the electromagnet delays sphere release making the recorded fall time too large and producing a systematic underestimate of g.

options.label: A
options.text: A denser sphere falls faster solely because gravitational field strength g increases with mass.
options.distractorRationale: In vacuum all masses accelerate at g = 9.81 m s⁻²; density merely makes air drag negligible compared to weight.

options.label: B
options.text: A larger hollow ball reduces drag because its greater surface area stabilises the wake.
options.distractorRationale: Larger cross-sectional area increases drag while smaller mass lowers weight, increasing deceleration.

options.label: C
options.text: Air resistance causes an overestimate of g because the sphere takes longer to hit the trapdoor.
options.distractorRationale: Longer fall time t reduces 2h/t², causing an underestimate of g.

options.label: D
options.text: High weight-to-drag ratio keeps air resistance negligible; alongside air drag, residual magnetism in the electromagnet delays sphere release making the recorded fall time too large and producing a systematic underestimate of g.

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a gymnasium scoreboard suspension beam of total length L = 4.4 m and mass 32 kg hangs horizontally in equilibrium from two light ceiling wires attached at A and B (3.8 m apart), with wire An inclined at 50° above the horizontal bar. Its centre of gravity G lies 2.43 m to the right of attachment A and 1.37 m to the left of attachment B (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the tension in wire B (T₂)?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about B: T₁_y × 3.8 = 32 × 9.81 × 1.37 ⇒ T₁_y = 113.2 N, T₂_y = 200.7 N. With wire A at 50°, T₁ = T₁_y / sin 50° = 147.7 N ≈ 148 N, horizontal component H = T₁ cos 50° = 94.97 N, and T₂ = √(H² + T₂_y²) = 222.1 N ≈ 222 N.

markScheme.criterion: Correct wire tension = 222 N.

items.stem: Two equal and opposite parallel forces, each of magnitude F = 18 N, are applied to the ends of a water-main gate-valve handwheel spar of length d = 0.4 m, acting perpendicularly to the bar, as illustrated in the diagram. What is the magnitude of the torque of this couple?
items.workedSolution: Torque of a couple = F × perpendicular separation = 18 × 0.4 = 7.200 N m ≈ 7.20 N m.

markScheme.criterion: Correct couple torque = 7.20 N m.

items.stem: Of weight 1360 N, a freight container sled descends a dockyard unloading ramp at steady speed over a slope distance of 11 m through a vertical height change of 3.1 m. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 1360 × 3.1 = 4.22 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 383 N. Target = 4.22 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 3.1/11 and zero net force to obtain 4.22 × 10³ J (C).

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a café awning horizontal support rod is a uniform horizontal rod of length L = 2.8 m and mass 7 kg smoothly hinged to a vertical wall at O. A rectangular sign of mass 10 kg hangs so that its centre of gravity acts 2.5 m from O. A taut support wire joins the outer end of the rod to the wall at an angle of 46° above the horizontal rod (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Moments about O give T = 169.5 N ≈ 169 N. (b) Horizontal balance: R_x = T cos θ = 117.7 N ≈ 118 N. (c) Vertical balance: R_y = W_total − T sin θ = 44.85 N ≈ 44.8 N.

Evaluates T = 169.5 N (169 N) showing agreement with 1.7e+2 N.
Applies horizontal equilibrium R_x = T cos θ.
R_x = 118 N away from the wall.
Applies vertical equilibrium R_y = W_total − T sin θ.
R_y = 44.8 N upwards.

parts.prompt: By taking moments about hinge O, show clearly that the tension T in the angled wire is approximately 1.7e+2 N.
workingSteps: Clockwise moment about O = (7 × 1.4 + 10 × 2.5) × 9.81 = 341.4 N m.
T = 169.5 N ≈ 169 N, which rounds to 1.7e+2 N.

parts.prompt: Calculate the horizontal component of the force exerted by hinge O on the rod.
workingSteps: Horizontal equilibrium: R_x = T cos 46° = 169.5 × cos 46° = 117.7 N ≈ 118 N away from the wall.

parts.prompt: Calculate the vertical component of the force exerted by hinge O on the rod.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium: R_y = W − T sin 46° = 44.85 N ≈ 44.8 N upwards.

items.stem: During Required Practical 4 on a hard-drawn steel wire of length $L = 2.40$ m, three micrometer diameter pairs average to 0.42 mm, 0.44 mm, and 0.43 mm. The linear elastic graph of force $F$ against extension $e$ has gradient 12.1 N mm⁻¹. Determine the Young modulus $E$ in GPa.
items.workedSolution: Mean diameter $d = 0.43$ mm gives $A = \pi d^2/4 = 1.45 × 10⁻⁷ m²$. $E = L \times \mathrm{grad} / A = 200 GPa$. Percentage uncertainty $\%\Delta E = \%\Delta L + 2\%\Delta d + \%\Delta\mathrm{grad} = 0.0833 + 2(2.33) + 2 = 6.73%$.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly evaluates youngModulusGPa $= 200 GPa$.

items.stem: Two coaxial clutch discs on a frictionless vertical shaft have moments of inertia $I_1 = 0.750 kg m²$ (spinning at 48.0 rad s⁻¹) and $I_2 = 1.25 kg m²$ (initially at rest). The discs engage and reach a common angular speed after slipping for 0.600 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) $\omega_{\mathrm{f}} = 18.0 rad s⁻¹$. (b) Mean clutch torque $= \frac{I_2|\omega_{\mathrm{f}} - \omega_2|}{\Delta t} = 37.5 N m$. (c) Energy dissipated $= 540 J$ as heat from sliding friction.

markScheme.criterion: Applies conservation of angular momentum $(I_1 + I_2)\omega_{\mathrm{f}} = I_1\omega_1 + I_2\omega_2$.
Obtains $\omega_{\mathrm{f}} = 18.0 rad s⁻¹$.
Applies angular impulse $T\Delta t = \Delta(I_2\omega_2)$.
Obtains mean torque $= 37.5 N m$.
Computes both initial and final total rotational kinetic energy.
Obtains energy loss $= 540 J$.
States that energy is dissipated as thermal energy due to friction while the plates slip.

parts.prompt: Calculate the common angular velocity of the coupled discs.
workingSteps: Conserve angular momentum: $(I_1 + I_2)\omega_{\mathrm{f}} = I_1\omega_1 + I_2\omega_2$.

parts.prompt: Calculate the mean friction torque exerted on Disc 2 during the slipping interval.
workingSteps: Angular impulse on Disc 2 is $I_2|\omega_{\mathrm{f}} - \omega_2| = 22.5 N m s$.
Divide by $\Delta t = 0.600 s$ to obtain $T = 37.5 N m$.

parts.prompt: Calculate the rotational kinetic energy lost during engagement and explain physically what happens to it.
parts.expectedAnswer: 540 J; kinetic energy decreases because thermal energy is dissipated by friction between slipping clutch plates.
workingSteps: Initial KE $= 864 J$, final KE $= 324 J$.
Energy lost $= 540 J$, dissipated as thermal energy by sliding friction between the clutch surfaces.

items.stem: A 980 kg electric shuttle carries a KERS flywheel of moment of inertia 2.50 kg m² whose speed must not fall below 180 rad s⁻¹ after climbing a 19.0 m vertical rise along a 180 m slope against 195 N mean drag. Using $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the minimum initial angular speed of the flywheel at the foot of the slope.
items.workedSolution: Total climb energy $E = 980(9.81)(19.0) + 195(180) = 2.18 × 10⁵ J$. From $\frac{1}{2}I(\omega_{\max}^2 - \omega_{\min}^2) = E$, $\omega_{\max} = \sqrt{180^2 + \frac{2E}{2.50}} = 455 rad s⁻¹$.

markScheme.criterion: Minimum initial angular speed equals 455 rad s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the flywheel slows all the way to rest instead of retaining $180\text{ rad s}^{-1}$.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds $\omega_{\min}$ outside the square root instead of inside $\sqrt{\omega_{\min}^2 + 2E/I}$.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Introduces an erroneous factor of one-half during rearrangement.

items.stem: A foundry ingot sled (weight 1150 N) slides at constant speed 6.5 m s⁻¹ down a refractory cooling chute, which is 22 m long and drops 11 m vertically. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1150 × (11/22) = 575 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 3.74 × 10³ W. Target = 575 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 575 N (D).

items.stem: Held with its 1.4 m light string horizontal in a suspension test gantry, an instrumented pendulum mass (2.5 kg) swings down from rest and sticks to stationary a magnetic-latch block (5.5 kg) at the lowest point. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the speed of the coupled bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.24 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 73.6 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.64 m s⁻¹. Target = 1.64 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 1.64 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: In a laboratory swing frame, a brass impact sphere of mass 1 kg attached to a light inextensible string of length 2.2 m is released from rest with the string horizontal. At the lowest point of its swing it collides with and sticks to stationary a wax capture block of mass 1.2 kg. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mgL = ½mu² => u = √(2gL).
Obtains 6.57 m s⁻¹.
Finds v = mu/(m+M) from momentum conservation and evaluates ½mu² − ½(m+M)v².
Obtains 11.8 J.
Applies h = v² / (2g).
Obtains 0.455 m.

items.stem: The diagram shows the rotor of a workshop pottery wheel test rig. Its central hub has moment of inertia 0.650 kg m² and carries 4 rim masses of 1.25 kg each at radius 0.400 m. During a test run lasting 8.00 s, the rotational speed changes uniformly from 3.00 rev s⁻¹ to 11.0 rev s⁻¹ while a constant bearing friction torque of 1.40 N m opposes rotation.
items.workedSolution: (a) $I = 1.45 kg m²$. (b) $|\alpha| = \frac{2\pi|f_2 - f_1|}{t} = 6.28 rad s⁻²$. (c) Applied torque $T_{\mathrm{app}} = 10.5 N m$. (d) Peak power $P_{\max} = T_{\mathrm{app}}\omega_{\max} = 726 W$.

markScheme.criterion: Uses $I = I_{\mathrm{hub}} + \sum m r^2$ with squared radius.
Obtains $I = 1.45 kg m²$.
Converts $\text{rev s}^{-1}$ to $\text{rad s}^{-1}$ via $2\pi$ and divides change by $t$.
Obtains $|\alpha| = 6.28 rad s⁻²$.
Combines $I|\alpha|$ with bearing friction torque in the correct sense.
Obtains applied torque $= 10.5 N m$.
Applies $P = T\omega$ at the highest angular speed.
Obtains maximum power $= 726 W$.

items.stem: Along a planar terminal slide inclined at 24° to the horizontal, a baggage transfer container (mass 10.5 kg) slides 8 m from rest and arrives at the base travelling at 4.39 m s⁻¹. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. How much mechanical energy is dissipated against friction during the descent?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 24° = 335 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(10.5)(4.39)² = 101 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 234 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 24°)L, μ = 0.311. Target = 234 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 24° accurately to obtain 234 J (C).

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a reinforced theatre stage drawbridge flap of length L = 2.4 m and mass 22 kg is smoothly hinged at O to a vertical wall and held horizontally in static equilibrium. Because of an internal reinforcing frame, its centre of gravity G lies 0.86 m from hinge O. A single steel cable attached to the outer edge pulls upward and toward the wall at an angle of 30° to the vertical (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the magnitude of the resultant reaction force R exerted on the door by hinge O?
items.workedSolution: Moments about O: T cos 30° × 2.4 = 22 × 9.81 × 0.86 ⇒ T = 89.30 N. Horizontal balance: R_x = T sin 30° = 44.65 N. Vertical balance: R_y = 22 × 9.81 − T cos 30° = 138.5 N. Resultant R = √(R_x² + R_y²) = 145.5 N ≈ 146 N, at angle α = tan⁻¹(R_y / R_x) = 72.13° ≈ 72.1° above the horizontal.

markScheme.criterion: Correct verified value = 146 N.

items.stem: In an overhead hoist beam, a crane overload test block (12 kg) falls from rest at the support through the 2 m slack length of an elastic snubber line to point A and is brought momentarily to rest after stretching 1.2 m in a time of 0.21 s to B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the time-averaged tension in an elastic snubber line during this 0.21 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2) = 6.26 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.21 + 12(9.81) = 476 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 476 N (C).

items.stem: Whirled in a vertical circle of radius 1.2 m on a light inextensible wire (breaking tension 38 N) in a vertical circular test rig, a steel sensor sphere has mass 0.8 kg. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the greatest safe speed at the lowest point.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((38/0.8) − 9.81) × 1.2] = 6.73 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 6.73 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: In an overhead hoist beam, a crane overload test block of mass 4.5 kg is released from rest at the upper support of an elastic snubber line, which has natural unstretched length 2.2 m and obeys Hooke's law when taut. The cord first becomes taut at A and reaches maximum extension 0.75 m at lowest point B after an arrest interval of 0.16 s. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses free-fall relation v_A = √(2gL).
Obtains 6.57 m s⁻¹.
Equates mg(L + x) = ½kx² over the complete vertical drop.
Obtains 463 N m⁻¹.
Evaluates a_B = (kx − mg) / m.
Obtains 67.4 m s⁻².
