items.stem: The horizontal boom of a shipyard steel-plate lifting crane has total length L = 25 m and mass 950 kg, supported on a vertical mast pivot P located 5 m from the rear end A. A concrete counterweight of mass 4000 kg sits 3.6 m to the left of P (1.4 m from A). The centre of gravity G of the boom itself lies 3 m to the right of P (8 m from A), and the hoist hook hangs 19.5 m to the right of P (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum safe load mass that can be suspended from the hook for rotational equilibrium about P?
items.workedSolution: Anticlockwise counterweight moment about P: M_cw = 4000 × 9.81 × 3.6 = 1.413 × 10⁵ N m. Clockwise boom moment: M_boom = 950 × 9.81 × 3 = 2.796 × 10⁴ N m. Remaining clockwise moment available for load: W_max × 19.5 = 1.133 × 10⁵ N m ⇒ W_max = 5811 N ≈ 5.81e+3 N, m_max = W_max / 9.81 = 592.3 kg ≈ 592 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Correct maximum safe load mass = 592 kg.

items.stem: Along a level low-friction dynamics rail, cart X of mass 2 kg travels to the right at 4 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary cart Y of mass 2 kg. Immediately after impact, cart Y moves to the right at 2.63 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies m_X u_X = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y.
Obtains 1.37 m s⁻¹.
Sums ½m_X v_X² + ½m_Y v_Y².
Obtains 8.79 J.
Subtracts K_f from K_i = ½m_X u_X².
Obtains 7.21 J.

items.stem: On a pitched workshop plank (7.5 m long, angled at 22° to the horizontal), a timber tool chest of mass 5.5 kg slides from rest and attains 4.45 m s⁻¹ at the base against constant kinetic friction. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. If the same object is instead released from rest halfway down a pitched workshop plank, what speed does it reach at the bottom?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 22° − ½mv² = 97.1 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 7.5 = 13.0 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.15 m s⁻¹. Target = 3.15 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 3.15 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Along a horizontal frictionless air track, glider X of mass 0.8 kg moves to the right at 7 m s⁻¹ and strikes stationary glider Y of mass 2.6 kg. Immediately after the collision, glider Y moves to the right at 2.67 m s⁻¹. Take rightward as positive.

markScheme.criterion: Applies signed momentum conservation m_X u_X = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y.
Obtains 1.68 m s⁻¹ to the left.
Adds positive scalar kinetic energies ½m_X v_X² + ½m_Y v_Y².
Obtains 10.4 J.
Evaluates K_i − K_f.
Obtains 9.21 J.

items.stem: In a vertical loop frame, a compact lead bob of mass 0.7 kg is attached to a light steel cable of length 0.8 m and moves in a vertical circle, passing through the lowest point with speed 7 m s⁻¹. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_c = mv² / r.
Obtains 42.9 N.
Applies T − mg = F_c => T = F_c + mg.
Obtains 49.7 N.

Hence calculate the tension in a light steel cable at the lowest point.

items.stem: A hail-impact test sphere leaves an angled gas gun at 18 m s⁻¹ inclined at 55° above the horizontal over a horizontal test hall. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test hall does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 55° = 10.3 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 55°)² / (2g) = 11.1 m. Target = 11.1 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 55° at apex to obtain 11.1 m (D).

options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: In a workshop statics test, a workshop bench-testing steel bar AB of length L = 3.2 m and mass 18 kg has its centre of gravity G at 2.05 m from end A. It is balanced horizontally on a knife-edge pivot P located 1.02 m from end A by placing a 26 kg calibration block to the left of P (use g = 9.81 m s⁻²). How far from end B must the 26 kg block be positioned for horizontal equilibrium?
items.workedSolution: Distance of CG from pivot P: d_G = 2.05 − 1.02 = 1.030 m. Taking moments about P: 26 × d = 18 × 1.030 ⇒ d = 0.7131 m left of P. Position from end A is x_A = 1.02 − 0.7131 = 0.3069 m. Therefore distance from end B is L − x_A = 3.2 − 0.3069 = 2.893 m ≈ 2.89 m.

markScheme.criterion: Correct distance from end B = 2.89 m.

items.stem: Along a polished ice test channel, sled X of mass 4 kg travelling right at 11 m s⁻¹ meets sled Y of mass 2.4 kg travelling left at 5 m s⁻¹ (not drawn). After impact sled Y rebounds right at 3 m s⁻¹. What is the post-collision velocity of sled X?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(11) + (2.4)(−5) = 32.0 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (2.4)(3), v_X = 6.20 m s⁻¹, which is 6.20 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 32.0 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 6.20 m s⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a park footbridge inspection deck of total length L = 7 m and mass 28 kg rests horizontally on two narrow supports A and B. Support A is positioned 0.8 m from its left end, and support B is 4.2 m to the right of A, leaving an unsupported right-hand overhang of 2 m. A technician of mass 58 kg initially stands 3.5 m from the left end of the plank (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). If the technician steps off and a toolbox is placed right at the outer overhanging tip, what is the maximum toolbox mass the plank can support without tipping?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about B: F₁ × 4.2 = (28 × 1.500 + 58 × 1.500) × 9.81 ⇒ F₁ = 301.3 N ≈ 301 N. At tipping (F₁ = 0): m_load × d_tip = m_beam × (x_B − x_G) ⇒ d_tip = (28 × 1.500) / 58 = 0.7241 m ≈ 0.724 m. At the very tip (overhang 2 m): m_end = (28 × 1.500) / 2 = 21.00 kg ≈ 21.0 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Correct solver-verified answer = 21.0 kg.

items.stem: On a horizontal test hall, an angled gas gun launches a hail-impact test sphere from ground level at speed 38 m s⁻¹ and angle 22° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates u_y = u sin θ.
Obtains 14.2 m s⁻¹.
Applies T = 2u_y / g.
Obtains 2.90 s.
Multiplies u cos θ by flight time T.
Obtains 102 m.

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a mine-tunnel shuttle vehicle of mass 1600 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling pendulum sensor hangs at 34° to the vertical, later climbs a 8° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 80 m (static friction coefficient 0.8), and coasts from 18 m s⁻¹ against a 350 N resistive force toward the shaft station. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a ceiling pendulum sensor deflects by 34°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 34° = ma and T cos 34° = mg => a = g tan 34° = 6.62 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.8 × 9.81 × 80) = 25.1 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1600)(18)² / 350 = 741 m. Target = 6.62 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 6.62 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: Shortly after opening a parachute, an $85.0\text{ kg}$ skydiver experiences an upward air resistance of $1340\text{ N}$. Taking $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the magnitude of the skydiver's upward deceleration.
items.workedSolution: Weight $W = 85.0 \times 9.81 = 833.9\text{ N}$; upward resultant force $F = 1340 - 833.9 = 506.1\text{ N}$; deceleration $a = F/m = 5.95 m s⁻²$. Option B (5.95 m s⁻²) matches.

markScheme.criterion: Upward deceleration $= 5.95 m s⁻²$ (5.95 m s⁻², option B).

items.stem: A uniform steel-fibre concrete tie beam of length L = 3.40 m rests horizontally on level ground (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). As shown in the figure, it has a rectangular cross-section of width w = 25.0 cm and thickness h = 12.0 cm and average density ρ = 2520 kg m⁻³. The component is uniform along its length so its centre of gravity G lies at its midpoint. A prefabrication hall hoist rated at electrical input power 820 W and efficiency 85% is later attached to end B to stand the component vertically upright on end A.
items.workedSolution: (a) A = 0.03000 m², V = A L = 0.1020 m³, m = ρ V = 257.0 kg ≈ 257 kg. (b) W = 2522 N; taking moments about A gives F = W × (x_G / L) = 1261 N ≈ 1.26e+3 N. (c) Centre of gravity rises by Δh = 1.700 m, so ΔE_p = m g Δh = 4287 J ≈ 4.29e+3 J. (d) Useful power P_out = 0.85 × 820 = 697.0 W, so t = 4287 / 697.0 = 6.150 s ≈ 6.15 s. (e) electrical heating in the motor windings and friction in the hoist gears dissipate thermal energy to the surroundings.

markScheme.criterion: Calculates cross-section A = 0.03000 m², volume V = 0.1020 m³, and applies m = ρ V.
Shows 4 s.f. mass 257.0 kg confirming 257 kg.
Applies principle of moments about A: F × 3.40 = m g × 1.700.
Evaluates minimum lift force F = 1.26e+3 N (4 s.f. 1261 N).
Uses centre-of-gravity rise Δh = 1.700 m (not full length L) in ΔE_p = m g Δh.
Obtains work done = 4.29e+3 J (4 s.f. 4287 J).
Applies useful power P_out = η P_in = 697.0 W and t = ΔE_p / P_out.
Evaluates minimum hoist time = 6.15 s (4 s.f. 6.150 s).
Identifies electrical heating in motor windings and mechanical friction in hoist gears.
Links losses to thermal energy dissipated to the surroundings (electrical heating in the motor windings and friction in the hoist gears dissipate thermal energy to the surroundings).

By taking moments about end A, calculate the minimum vertical upward force F applied at end B required to just lift end B off the ground. [2]

Neglecting the initial height of the centre of gravity above the ground, calculate the minimum work done (gain in gravitational potential energy) to rotate the component until it stands vertically upright on end A. [2]
workingSteps: Vertical rise of centre of gravity G is Δh = L / 2 = 1.700 m

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum time taken for the 820 W hoist motor operating at 85% efficiency to stand the component upright. [2]
workingSteps: Useful output power P_out = η P_in = 0.85 × 820 = 697.0 W

parts.expectedAnswer: electrical heating in the motor windings and friction in the hoist gears dissipate thermal energy to the surroundings.

items.stem: A taper-reinforced concrete kerb beam of length L = 3.00 m rests horizontally on level ground (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). As shown in the figure, it has a rectangular cross-section of width w = 20.0 cm and thickness h = 15.0 cm and average density ρ = 2450 kg m⁻³. Internal reinforcement makes the component non-uniform so its centre of gravity G lies at distance x = 1.29 m from end A (as shown). A roadworks lifting winch rated at electrical input power 640 W and efficiency 77% is later attached to end B to stand the component vertically upright on end A.
items.workedSolution: (a) A = 0.03000 m², V = A L = 0.09000 m³, m = ρ V = 220.5 kg ≈ 221 kg. (b) W = 2163 N; taking moments about A gives F = W × (x_G / L) = 930.1 N ≈ 930 N. (c) Centre of gravity rises by Δh = 1.290 m, so ΔE_p = m g Δh = 2790 J ≈ 2.79e+3 J. (d) Useful power P_out = 0.77 × 640 = 492.8 W, so t = 2790 / 492.8 = 5.662 s ≈ 5.66 s. (e) density is uniform and negligible work is done against friction or giving kinetic energy to the beam.

Calculates V = A L = 0.09000 m³ and substitutes m = ρ V.
Shows 4 s.f. mass 220.5 kg rounding clearly to 221 kg.
Applies principle of moments about A: F × 3.00 = m g × 1.290.
Evaluates minimum lift force F = 930 N (4 s.f. 930.1 N).
Uses centre-of-gravity rise Δh = 1.290 m (not full length L) in ΔE_p = m g Δh.
Obtains work done = 2.79e+3 J (4 s.f. 2790 J).
Applies useful power P_out = η P_in = 492.8 W and t = ΔE_p / P_out.
Evaluates minimum hoist time = 5.66 s (4 s.f. 5.662 s).
States valid physical assumption: density is uniform and negligible work is done against friction or giving kinetic energy to the beam.

items.stem: Why is dropping a sphere through two light gates superior to dropping from a hand-held release onto a single trapdoor in RP3?
items.workedSolution: RP3 evaluation: Starting timing electronically at Gate 1 avoids release-delay errors, while students use a plumb line to align the metre ruler vertically and plot two h over t against t so the gradient equals gravitational field strength independently of initial speed.

markScheme.criterion: Starting timing electronically at Gate 1 avoids release-delay errors, while students use a plumb line to align the metre ruler vertically and plot two h over t against t so the gradient equals gravitational field strength independently of initial speed.

items.stem: In an electromagnet-and-trapdoor free-fall experiment (RP3), a steel sphere falls from rest through height $h = 1.45$ m. Because residual magnetism delays release by 11 ms, the electronic timer records 0.5547 s. What apparent value of $g$ is calculated from $h = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$?
items.workedSolution: $g_{\mathrm{apparent}} = 2h / t^2 = 2(1.45) / (0.5547)^2 = 9.42 m s⁻²$, systematically below 9.81 m s⁻² because the timer started before the ball detached.

markScheme.criterion: Calculates $g = 9.42 m s⁻²$.

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a train-concourse timetable carrier bar of total length L = 3.2 m and mass 14 kg hangs horizontally in equilibrium from two light vertical ceiling wires attached at A and B, separated by 2.4 m. Its centre of gravity G lies 0.72 m to the right of attachment A and 1.68 m to the left of attachment B (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Moments about B yield T₁ = 96.14 N ≈ 96.1 N. (b) Force balance gives T₂ = 41.20 N ≈ 41.2 N. (c) wire A carries the greater tension because the centre of gravity is closer to wire A.

markScheme.criterion: Applies moment balance about attachment B.
Applies ΣF_y = 0 to obtain T₂.
Identifies the wire closer to G as carrying greater tension.
Justifies using equal opposite moments about G with shorter lever arm.

workingSteps: Since wire A is vertical, T₁ = 96.14 N ≈ 96.1 N.

parts.prompt: Using vertical force equilibrium, determine the tension T₂ in wire B.
State which wire carries the greater tension and justify your answer qualitatively in terms of moments about the centre of gravity.
parts.expectedAnswer: In equilibrium, wire A carries the greater tension because the centre of gravity is closer to wire A.
workingSteps: Take moments about the centre of gravity so the weight has zero moment.
Show that the wire with the shorter perpendicular distance to G must exert the larger tension to balance moments.

items.stem: Two equal and opposite parallel forces, each of magnitude F = 62 N, are applied to the ends of an aircraft trim-wheel control bar of length d = 0.68 m, acting perpendicularly to the bar, as illustrated in the diagram.
items.workedSolution: A rigid body is in equilibrium when it has zero resultant force and zero resultant moment about any point.

markScheme.criterion: Zero resultant force (translational equilibrium).
Zero resultant moment about any point (rotational equilibrium).

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a bakery timber fascia sign rod is a uniform horizontal rod of length L = 2.8 m and mass 8 kg smoothly hinged to a vertical wall at O. A rectangular sign of mass 4.5 kg hangs so that its centre of gravity acts 2.4 m from O. A taut support wire joins the outer end of the rod to the wall at an angle of 54° above the horizontal rod (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the horizontal component of force exerted on the rod by hinge O?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about hinge O: T sin 54° × 2.8 = (8 × 1.4 + 4.5 × 2.4) × 9.81 = 215.8 N m. Hence T sin 54° = 77.08 N and T = 95.27 N ≈ 95.3 N. Horizontal balance: R_x = T cos 54° = 56.00 N ≈ 56.0 N. Vertical balance: R_y = (8 + 4.5) × 9.81 − 77.08 = 45.55 N ≈ 45.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Correct verified value = 56.0 N.

items.stem: In Searle's Young modulus investigation (RP4) on a yellow brass wire of unstretched length $(1.90 \pm 0.001)$ m, micrometer diameter measurements at three orthogonal positions average to 0.36 mm, 0.38 mm, and 0.37 mm (each $\pm 0.01$ mm). Plotting load $F$ against extension $e$ yields a straight line through the origin of gradient 5.7 N mm⁻¹ ($\pm 2.4\%$).
items.workedSolution: (a) $A = \pi d^2/4 = 1.08 × 10⁻⁷ m²$. (b) $E = L(\mathrm{grad})/A = 101 GPa$. (c) $\%\Delta E = 7.86%$. (d) an identical reference wire compensates both ceiling sag and thermal expansion while orthogonal micrometer diameter measurements reduce cross sectional area uncertainty.

markScheme.criterion: Averages three diameters and converts mm to m in $A = \pi d^2/4$.
Cross-sectional area $A = 1.08 × 10⁻⁷ m²$.
Converts gradient to N m⁻¹ and substitutes into $E = (L/A)\,\mathrm{grad}$.
Young modulus $E = 101 GPa$.
Combines $\%\Delta L + 2\%\Delta d + \%\Delta\mathrm{grad}$.
Percentage uncertainty in $E = 7.86%$.
Identical reference wire compensates both support sag and temperature expansion.
Orthogonal micrometer readings at >= 3 positions detect non-uniformity/oval cross-section.

Determine the Young modulus $E$ of the wire in GPa.
Calculate the percentage uncertainty in $E$.
Explain the purpose of the reference wire and why orthogonal micrometer readings are taken at three places.
parts.expectedAnswer: an identical reference wire compensates both ceiling sag and thermal expansion while orthogonal micrometer diameter measurements reduce cross sectional area uncertainty
workingSteps: Identical reference wire cancels ceiling sag and thermal expansion equally on both scales.
Orthogonal readings at 3 positions check circularity and reduce random error in d².

items.stem: A reversing mill drum of moment of inertia 2.50 kg m² initially turns clockwise at $+16.0\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. A steady reversing torque brings it to $-12.0\text{ rad s}^{-1}$ (anticlockwise). Calculate the magnitude of the angular impulse delivered to the drum.
items.workedSolution: Angular impulse $T\Delta t = \Delta(I\omega) = I(\omega_2 - \omega_1) = 2.50(-12.0 - 16.0) = -70.0\text{ N m s}$. Its magnitude is 70.0 N m s.

markScheme.criterion: Magnitude of angular impulse equals 70.0 N m s.

items.stem: Engineers evaluate a composite flywheel of moment of inertia 5.40 kg m² operating between 180 rad s⁻¹ and 156 rad s⁻¹ inside a backup generator set of total mass 1.05e+3 kg. On a test incline of road length 160 m rising 11.0 m vertically, the mean resistive drag force is 175 N. Take $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
items.workedSolution: (a) $\Delta E_{\mathrm{k}} = 2.18 × 10⁴ J$. (b) $\Delta E_{\mathrm{p}} = 1.13 × 10⁵ J$. (c) Subtracting drag work 2.80 × 10⁴ J and dividing by $mg$ gives $h_{\max} = 0 m$.

markScheme.criterion: Uses $\Delta E_{\mathrm{k}} = \frac{1}{2}I(\omega_{\max}^2 - \omega_{\min}^2)$.
Obtains 2.18 × 10⁴ J.
Uses $mgh$ with $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Obtains 1.13 × 10⁵ J.
Computes drag work $F_{\mathrm{d}}s$ and subtracts from flywheel energy release.
Equates remaining energy to $mg h_{\max}$.
Obtains $h_{\max} = 0 m$.

parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy released by the flywheel as it slows across its operating speed range.
Calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy during the test incline.
workingSteps: Use $\Delta E_{\mathrm{p}} = m g \Delta h$ with $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.prompt: Assuming zero transmission losses and constant resistive work along the same road length, determine the maximum vertical height this flywheel energy release could lift the vehicle.
workingSteps: Work against drag $W_{\mathrm{d}} = F_{\mathrm{d}} s = 2.80 × 10⁴ J$.
Remaining energy for height gain $mgh_{\max} = \Delta E_{\mathrm{k}} - W_{\mathrm{d}}$.

Obtains 700 N.
Applies P = F_f v.
Obtains 4.55 × 10³ W.

items.stem: The diagram shows a steel pendulum bob of mass 0.8 kg swinging from a horizontal 1.5 m string in a ballistic pendulum rig to couple with stationary a lump of modelling clay of mass 2 kg at the lowest point. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above the lowest point do the joined bodies reach?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 5.42 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 1.55 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.122 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 8.41 J. Target = 0.122 m.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 0.122 m (B).

items.stem: A spoked rotor (hub inertia 0.80 kg m² plus 4 rim masses of 1.10 kg each at radius 0.50 m) is accelerated uniformly from 4.0 rev s⁻¹ to 16.0 rev s⁻¹ in 10.0 s against a constant bearing friction torque of 2.20 N m. Calculate the driving torque supplied by the motor.
items.workedSolution: Total inertia $I = 0.80 + 4(1.10)(0.50)^2 = 1.90\text{ kg m}^2$. Angular acceleration $\alpha = \frac{2\pi(16.0 - 4.0)}{10.0} = 7.54\text{ rad s}^{-2}$. Driving torque $T_{\mathrm{app}} = I\alpha + T_{\mathrm{f}} = (1.90 \times 7.54) + 2.20 = 16.5 N m$.

markScheme.criterion: Applied driving torque equals 16.5 N m.

items.stem: Starting from rest at the top of a tilted discharge chute of length 10 m inclined at 36° to the horizontal, a cast-iron foundry billet of mass 8 kg slides to the bottom where its speed is 5.91 m s⁻¹. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance.

Obtains 461 J.

Obtains 322 J.
Applies W_f = μ(mg cos θ)L.

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a hydro-station spillway hinged sluice flap of length L = 1.8 m and mass 30 kg is smoothly hinged at O to a vertical wall and held horizontally in static equilibrium. Because of an internal reinforcing frame, its centre of gravity G lies 0.83 m from hinge O. A single steel cable attached to the outer edge pulls upward and toward the wall at an angle of 24° to the vertical (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 148.5 N ≈ 149 N. (b) the angled wire exerts a horizontal component pulling toward the wall so the hinge must provide an equal horizontal force away from the wall for translational equilibrium. (c)(i) R_x = 60.42 N, R_y = 158.6 N, so R = 169.7 N ≈ 170 N. (c)(ii) α = tan⁻¹(R_y / R_x) = 69.14° ≈ 69.1° above the horizontal.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Στ = 0 about O using T cos(angle to vertical) × L = m g x_G.
Obtains T = 148.5 N (149 N) matching 1.5e+2 N.
Identifies horizontal component of angled cable tension directed toward the wall.
States hinge must exert an equal opposite horizontal force away from the wall for ΣF_x = 0.
Computes R_x = 60.42 N and R_y = 158.6 N and applies Pythagoras.
Resultant hinge reaction magnitude R = 170 N.
Uses tan α = R_y / R_x with both hinge components.
Direction α = 69.1° above the horizontal.

items.stem: Released from rest at the anchor of a stretchable nylon hawser (natural length 2.6 m) in a dry-test tower, a marine mooring weight of mass 5 kg falls freely to point A where the cord becomes taut, then stretches the cord by 1.2 m over 0.18 s before reaching instantaneous rest at B. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates v_A = √(2gL).
Obtains 7.14 m s⁻¹.
Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = m v_A, including weight mg.
Mean resultant upward force = (5 × 7.14) / 0.18 = 198 N.
Obtains 247 N.
Uses mg(L + x) = ½kx² and T_B = kx.
Obtains 311 N.

items.stem: Attached to a braided dynamic lanyard of unstretched length 4 m in a fall-arrest gantry, a rescue arrest dummy of mass 2.5 kg falls from rest at the anchor, passes taut point A, and stretches the cord by 0.45 m in 0.34 s to rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the peak tension in a braided dynamic lanyard at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 4 + 0.45 = 4.45 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 1.08 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 485 N. Target = 485 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (4 + 0.45) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 485 N (C).

items.stem: The horizontal boom of a precast-concrete yard tower jib has total length L = 22 m and mass 1200 kg, supported on a vertical mast pivot P located 5.5 m from the rear end A. A concrete counterweight of mass 3800 kg sits 4.1 m to the left of P (1.4 m from A). The centre of gravity G of the boom itself lies 4 m to the right of P (9.5 m from A), and the hoist hook hangs 14 m to the right of P (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) M_cw = 1.528 × 10⁵ N m ≈ 1.53 × 10⁵ N m. (b) Equating clockwise and anticlockwise moments about P gives m_max = 770.0 kg ≈ 770 kg. (c) Vertical force balance yields R = 5.660 × 10⁴ N ≈ 5.66 × 10⁴ N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses M = m g d with counterweight mass and lever arm from P.
Counterweight moment = 1.53 × 10⁵ N m.
Subtracts boom self-weight moment from counterweight moment and divides by g × load lever arm.
Maximum safe load mass = 770 kg.
Applies vertical force balance summing counterweight, boom, and load weights.
Upward mast reaction R = 5.66 × 10⁴ N.

items.stem: During an inelastic collision trial on a level docking-simulator rail, module X (mass 5.2 kg, initial rightward speed 14 m s⁻¹) hits stationary module Y (mass 1.2 kg), which moves off to the right at 14.4 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of module X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (5.2)(14) = (5.2)v_X + (1.2)(14.4), giving v_X = 10.7 m s⁻¹. K_i = 510 J and K_f = 421 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 88.8 J. Target = 10.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 10.7 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Released from rest at the top of a refractory unloading ramp of length 6 m inclined at 22° to the horizontal, a ceramic kiln brick of mass 16 kg slides against a constant friction force and reaches the bottom at 3.65 m s⁻¹. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates mgL sin θ − ½mv².
Obtains 246 J.
Divides dissipated energy from (a) by ramp length L.
Obtains 41.0 N.

items.stem: The diagram shows shuttle X of mass 2 kg approaching stationary shuttle Y of mass 6.4 kg at 9 m s⁻¹ on a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway. After impact, shuttle Y moves right at 3.62 m s⁻¹. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (2)(9) = (2)v_X + (6.4)(3.62) gives v_X = -2.58 m s⁻¹ (2.58 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(2)(2.58)² + ½(6.4)(3.62)² = 48.6 J. Energy lost = 81.0 J − K_f = 32.4 J. Target = 32.4 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.58 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 32.4 J (D).

items.stem: The diagram shows a steel sensor sphere of mass 0.7 kg moving at 6.5 m s⁻¹ through the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.7 m on a light inextensible wire in a vertical circular test rig. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What tension acts in a light inextensible wire?
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 0.7 × 6.5² / 1.7 = 17.4 N, so T = 17.4 + 0.7 × 9.8 = 24.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 24.3 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

Obtains 35.8 m.
Evaluates R = u_x × (2u_y / g).
Obtains 76.1 m.

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, an architectural studio cantilever model AB of total length L = 4.6 m and mass 13 kg is uniform, with its centre of gravity G at its midpoint (2.3 m from end A). The beam rests horizontally in equilibrium on a sharp pivot P positioned 1.84 m from end A when a counterbalance block of unknown mass is placed 0.46 m from end A (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) The moment of a force about a pivot is the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action. (b) Taking moments about P: m_load g (1.380) = (13) g (0.4600), giving m_load = 4.333 kg ≈ 4.33 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Product of force and distance from the pivot.
Specifies perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force.
Equates opposing moments about P using d_G = 0.4600 m and d_load = 1.380 m.
Obtains balancing mass m = 4.33 kg (4 s.f. 4.333 kg).

items.stem: On a precision gas-bearing trough, rider X of mass 2.5 kg moves to the right at 10 m s⁻¹ and collides head-on with rider Y of mass 2.4 kg moving to the left at 6 m s⁻¹ (arrow on Y not shown). Immediately after impact, rider Y moves to the right at 3 m s⁻¹. Take motion to the right as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 2.5 × 10 + 2.4 × (−6) = 10.6 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 10.6 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (10.6 − 2.4 × 3) / 2.5 = 1.36 m s⁻¹. Answer: 1.36 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m_X u_X − m_Y |u_Y| with correct signs.
Obtains 10.6 kg m s⁻¹ to the right.
Solves p_before = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y for v_X.
Obtains 1.36 m s⁻¹ to the right.

items.workedSolution: (a) Moments about B give F₁ = 540.3 N ≈ 540 N. (b) Vertical equilibrium gives F₂ = 578.1 N ≈ 578 N. (c) the reaction force at support A decreases and the reaction force at support B increases. (d) Setting F₁ = 0 about B yields d_tip = 0.4364 m ≈ 0.436 m.

Support A reaction F₁ = 540 N.
Support B reaction F₂ = 578 N via vertical force balance.
States that the reaction force at support A decreases and the reaction force at support B increases.
Sets F₁ = 0 and equates clockwise overhang moment to restoring plank moment about B.
Tipping distance past B = 0.436 m.

parts.prompt: By taking moments about support B, calculate the upward reaction force F₁ at support A while the technician is at the initial position.
workingSteps: Clockwise moment of F₁ about B = F₁ × 2.8.

parts.prompt: Deduce the upward reaction force F₂ at support B.
State qualitatively how the reaction forces at supports A and B change as the technician walks slowly toward the right-hand overhang.
parts.expectedAnswer: As the technician moves toward the overhang, the reaction force at support A decreases and the reaction force at support B increases.
workingSteps: Explain that shifting weight toward support B reduces the anticlockwise moment about B so support A carries less load while support B carries more.

parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum distance past support B that the technician can walk onto the overhang before the plank begins to tip.
workingSteps: At the tipping limit, F₁ = 0; take moments about B: 66 g d_tip = 48 g (0.6000).

items.stem: During a range trial on a horizontal test paddock, a tracer polymer pellet leaves a ground discharge tube at 40 m s⁻¹ and 30° above the horizontal. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the total time of flight before returning to a horizontal test paddock?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 40 sin 30° = 20.0 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 40 cos 30° = 34.6 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 4.08 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 141 m. Target = 4.08 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 4.08 s (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: During proving-ground tests, an autonomous freight van of mass 1600 kg accelerates along a level straight so a cabin pendulum accelerometer deflects by 26° from the vertical, climbs a straight 8° incline at constant speed, negotiates a flat semicircular curve of radius 70 m (coefficient of static friction 0.6), and finally coasts along the semicircle from 18 m s⁻¹ against a constant 620 N resistance toward the inspection pad. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance.

markScheme.criterion: Uses T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg => a = g tan θ.
Obtains 4.78 m s⁻².
Applies μ_s mg = m v_max² / R.
Obtains 20.3 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts resistive work F_res(πR) from initial kinetic energy ½mu².
Obtains 12.4 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: By resolving forces on a cabin pendulum accelerometer, calculate the horizontal acceleration when the string deflects by 26°.
Calculate the maximum speed on the flat semicircular road without sliding.
Calculate the speed with which an autonomous freight van reaches the inspection pad at the end of the semicircular coast.

items.stem: The velocity–time graph shows the vertical descent of a skydiver from jumping out of a stationary balloon (origin), reaching free-fall terminal speed (Q), opening the parachute (R), and landing steadily at a lower terminal speed (S).
items.workedSolution: Level 3 (5–6 marks): Drag grows with speed until equal to weight at terminal velocity and opening the parachute creates an upward resultant force; systematically applies N2L ($F = mg - D = ma$) and N1L ($F = 0$) across release, curved acceleration P, first plateau Q, parachute deceleration R (still moving downwards!), and second lower plateau S.

markScheme.criterion: L1 (Area 1): At release (v = 0), drag is zero so resultant force equals weight mg and initial acceleration is g (steepest gradient).
L1 (Area 1): As speed increases (region P), upward air resistance increases, so downward resultant force (mg − D) and acceleration (gradient) decrease (Newton's 2nd law).
L2 (Area 2): At Q, upward drag equals constant downward weight so resultant force is zero.
L2 (Area 2): By Newton's 1st law, acceleration is zero and the skydiver falls at a constant high terminal velocity vT1.
L3 (Area 3): At R, opening the parachute increases surface area so drag greatly exceeds weight, creating an upward resultant force that decelerates the downward motion (N2L).
L3 (Area 3): As speed decreases, drag falls until drag equals weight again at S, establishing a much lower constant terminal velocity vT2.

parts.prompt: Explain the shape of the entire velocity–time graph from release to S using Newton's first and second laws of motion, referring explicitly to weight, air resistance, resultant force, and acceleration at each stage.
parts.expectedAnswer: At release ($t = 0$), speed and air resistance are zero, so the downward resultant force equals weight $mg$ and initial downward acceleration equals $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (steepest gradient, N2L). Drag grows with speed until equal to weight at terminal velocity and opening the parachute creates an upward resultant force: as speed rises through P, upward drag increases, reducing downward resultant force ($mg - D$) and acceleration so the curve gradient decreases. At Q, upward drag equals constant downward weight, resultant force is zero, and acceleration is zero so the skydiver falls at constant terminal velocity $v_{\text{T1}}$ (N1L). At R, opening the parachute greatly increases surface area and drag so $D \gg mg$, creating a large upward resultant force opposing downward velocity and causing rapid deceleration (N2L). As downward speed drops, drag decreases until $D = mg$ once more at S, giving a lower constant terminal speed $v_{\text{T2}}$.
workingSteps: Area 1 (L1): Initial release (v=0 -> D=0 -> a=g) and rising drag reducing downward resultant force and v-t gradient (N2L).
Area 2 (L2): First terminal velocity Q where drag = weight -> resultant force = 0 -> constant speed (N1L).
Area 3 (L3): Parachute opening R raises area -> D >> mg -> upward resultant force decelerates skydiver -> drag drops until D = mg at lower terminal speed S.

items.stem: A uniform precast foundation sill of length L = 3.50 m rests horizontally on level ground (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). As shown in the figure, it has a rectangular cross-section of width w = 24.0 cm and thickness h = 11.0 cm and average density ρ = 2360 kg m⁻³. The component is uniform along its length so its centre of gravity G lies at its midpoint. A site A-frame hoist motor rated at electrical input power 760 W and efficiency 79% is later attached to end B to stand the component vertically upright on end A.
items.workedSolution: (a) A = 0.02640 m², V = A L = 0.09240 m³, m = ρ V = 218.1 kg ≈ 218 kg. (b) W = 2139 N; taking moments about A gives F = W × (x_G / L) = 1070 N ≈ 1.07e+3 N. (c) Centre of gravity rises by Δh = 1.750 m, so ΔE_p = m g Δh = 3744 J ≈ 3.74e+3 J. (d) Useful power P_out = 0.79 × 760 = 600.4 W, so t = 3744 / 600.4 = 6.235 s ≈ 6.24 s. (e) electrical heating in the motor windings and friction in the hoist gears dissipate thermal energy to the surroundings.

markScheme.criterion: Calculates cross-section A = 0.02640 m², volume V = 0.09240 m³, and applies m = ρ V.
Shows 4 s.f. mass 218.1 kg confirming 218 kg.
Applies principle of moments about A: F × 3.50 = m g × 1.750.
Evaluates minimum lift force F = 1.07e+3 N (4 s.f. 1070 N).
Uses centre-of-gravity rise Δh = 1.750 m (not full length L) in ΔE_p = m g Δh.
Obtains work done = 3.74e+3 J (4 s.f. 3744 J).
Applies useful power P_out = η P_in = 600.4 W and t = ΔE_p / P_out.
Evaluates minimum hoist time = 6.24 s (4 s.f. 6.235 s).
Identifies electrical heating in motor windings and mechanical friction in hoist gears.
Links losses to thermal energy dissipated to the surroundings (electrical heating in the motor windings and friction in the hoist gears dissipate thermal energy to the surroundings).

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a theatre stage scenery fly-bar of total length L = 3.8 m and mass 14 kg hangs horizontally in equilibrium from two light vertical ceiling wires attached at A and B, separated by 3.1 m. Its centre of gravity G lies 2.23 m to the right of attachment A and 0.87 m to the left of attachment B (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the tension in wire B (T₂)?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about B: T₁_y × 3.1 = 14 × 9.81 × 0.87 ⇒ T₁_y = 38.54 N, T₂_y = 98.80 N. For vertical wires, T₁ = 38.54 N ≈ 38.5 N and T₂ = 98.80 N ≈ 98.8 N.

markScheme.criterion: Correct wire tension = 98.8 N.

items.stem: Two equal and opposite parallel forces, each of magnitude F = 50 N, are applied to the ends of a workshop tap-wrench turning bar of length d = 0.8 m, each inclined at 50° to the bar, as illustrated in the diagram. What is the magnitude of the torque of this couple?
items.workedSolution: Perpendicular separation between the parallel lines of action is d_perp = d sin 50° = 0.6128 m. Torque of the couple: T = F d_perp = 50 × 0.6128 = 30.64 N m ≈ 30.6 N m.

markScheme.criterion: Correct couple torque = 30.6 N m.

items.stem: In translational equilibrium at constant speed, a steel cable drum cradle (weight 120 N) travels 9 m down a warehouse ramp, dropping 4.3 m vertically. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 120 × 4.3 = 516 J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 57.3 N. Target = 516 J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 4.3/9 and zero net force to obtain 516 J (A).

items.stem: A uniform rectangular a theatre wing hinged fold-down table leaf of length L = 1 m and mass 13 kg is smoothly hinged along its left edge O to a vertical wall. It is held horizontally in equilibrium by a vertical upward force F applied at its outer edge 1 m from hinge O (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) F = ½ m g = 63.77 N ≈ 63.8 N. (b) Since R + F = W and R = 63.77 N, for a uniform horizontal flap only three vertical forces act and taking moments about the outer end shows the hinge supports half the weight.

markScheme.criterion: Applies principle of moments about O with CG at midpoint L/2.
States vertical equilibrium or moments about the outer edge.
Concludes the uniform weight is shared equally so hinge reaction equals half the weight.

workingSteps: Note that all forces acting on the uniform horizontal flap are purely vertical.

items.stem: Why do students record extension readings while both loading and unloading the test wire in Required Practical 4?
items.workedSolution: RP4 mark-scheme principle: Confirming unloading readings match loading readings verifies the elastic limit was not exceeded; meanwhile an identical reference wire compensates both ceiling sag and thermal expansion while orthogonal micrometer diameter measurements reduce cross sectional area uncertainty.

markScheme.criterion: Confirming unloading readings match loading readings verifies the elastic limit was not exceeded; meanwhile an identical reference wire compensates both ceiling sag and thermal expansion while orthogonal micrometer diameter measurements reduce cross sectional area uncertainty.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: Confirming unloading readings match loading readings verifies the elastic limit was not exceeded; meanwhile an identical reference wire compensates both ceiling sag and thermal expansion while orthogonal micrometer diameter measurements reduce cross sectional area uncertainty.

items.stem: Two coaxial clutch discs on a frictionless vertical shaft have moments of inertia $I_1 = 1.50 kg m²$ (spinning at 36.0 rad s⁻¹) and $I_2 = 0.900 kg m²$ (initially spinning at −12.0 rad s⁻¹). The discs engage and reach a common angular speed after slipping for 0.900 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) $\omega_{\mathrm{f}} = 18.0 rad s⁻¹$. (b) Mean clutch torque $= \frac{I_2|\omega_{\mathrm{f}} - \omega_2|}{\Delta t} = 30.0 N m$. (c) Energy dissipated $= 648 J$ as heat from sliding friction.

markScheme.criterion: Applies conservation of angular momentum $(I_1 + I_2)\omega_{\mathrm{f}} = I_1\omega_1 + I_2\omega_2$.
Obtains $\omega_{\mathrm{f}} = 18.0 rad s⁻¹$.
Applies angular impulse $T\Delta t = \Delta(I_2\omega_2)$.
Obtains mean torque $= 30.0 N m$.
Computes both initial and final total rotational kinetic energy.
Obtains energy loss $= 648 J$.
States that energy is dissipated as thermal energy due to friction while the plates slip.

items.stem: A single-cylinder generator engine is coupled to a cast-iron flywheel of moment of inertia 4.80 kg m². During each four-stroke cycle its angular speed fluctuates between 172 rad s⁻¹ and 148 rad s⁻¹. What energy is represented by the shaded area above the mean-load torque line on the turning-moment diagram?
items.workedSolution: The shaded energy loop equals the cyclic kinetic energy exchange $\Delta E = \frac{1}{2}I(\omega_{\max}^2 - \omega_{\min}^2) = \frac{1}{2}(4.80)(172^2 - 148^2) = 1.84 × 10⁴ J$.

markScheme.criterion: Cyclic flywheel energy exchange equals 1.84 × 10⁴ J.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Squares the speed difference instead of taking the difference of squares.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of one-half in $\frac{1}{2}I(\omega_{\max}^2 - \omega_{\min}^2)$.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes total stored kinetic energy rather than cyclic fluctuation energy.

items.stem: While sliding down a planar test embankment (32 m long, 9.6 m vertical height) at constant speed 5.5 m s⁻¹, a civil-engineering gabion of weight 850 N converts lost potential energy into heat. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 850 × (9.6/32) = 255 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.40 × 10³ W. Target = 255 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 255 N (D).

items.stem: In a Charpy-style swing rig, a cast-iron hammer bob of mass 1.7 kg hangs on a 2.2 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a deformable putty mass of mass 1.7 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a cast-iron hammer bob strikes a deformable putty mass?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 6.57 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 50.0 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 3.28 m s⁻¹. Target = 50.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 50.0 N (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows the rotor of an automated steel-shearing flywheel. Its central hub has moment of inertia 1.10 kg m² and carries 8 rim masses of 0.750 kg each at radius 0.500 m. During a test run lasting 12.0 s, the rotational speed changes uniformly from 5.00 rev s⁻¹ to 17.0 rev s⁻¹ while a constant bearing friction torque of 2.50 N m opposes rotation.
items.workedSolution: (a) $I = 2.60 kg m²$. (b) $|\alpha| = \frac{2\pi|f_2 - f_1|}{t} = 6.28 rad s⁻²$. (c) Applied torque $T_{\mathrm{app}} = 18.8 N m$. (d) Peak power $P_{\max} = T_{\mathrm{app}}\omega_{\max} = 2.01e+3 W$.

markScheme.criterion: Uses $I = I_{\mathrm{hub}} + \sum m r^2$ with squared radius.
Obtains $I = 2.60 kg m²$.
Converts $\text{rev s}^{-1}$ to $\text{rad s}^{-1}$ via $2\pi$ and divides change by $t$.
Obtains $|\alpha| = 6.28 rad s⁻²$.
Combines $I|\alpha|$ with bearing friction torque in the correct sense.
Obtains applied torque $= 18.8 N m$.
Applies $P = T\omega$ at the highest angular speed.
Obtains maximum power $= 2.01e+3 W$.

items.stem: During a surface-wear test on an anodized calibration incline (8.5 m long, 32° above the horizontal), an avionics shock canister of mass 14.5 kg slides from rest to a bottom speed of 6.3 m s⁻¹. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². How much mechanical energy is dissipated against friction during the descent?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 32° = 640 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(14.5)(6.3)² = 288 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 352 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 32°)L, μ = 0.344. Target = 352 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 32° accurately to obtain 352 J (A).

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a heavy non-uniform loft trapdoor of length L = 2.2 m and mass 28 kg is smoothly hinged at O to a vertical wall and held horizontally in static equilibrium. Because of an internal reinforcing frame, its centre of gravity G lies 0.79 m from hinge O. A single steel cable attached to the outer edge pulls upward and toward the wall at an angle of 38° to the vertical (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the magnitude of the resultant reaction force R exerted on the door by hinge O?
items.workedSolution: Moments about O: T cos 38° × 2.2 = 28 × 9.81 × 0.79 ⇒ T = 125.2 N. Horizontal balance: R_x = T sin 38° = 77.06 N. Vertical balance: R_y = 28 × 9.81 − T cos 38° = 176.0 N. Resultant R = √(R_x² + R_y²) = 192.2 N ≈ 192 N, at angle α = tan⁻¹(R_y / R_x) = 66.36° ≈ 66.4° above the horizontal.

markScheme.criterion: Correct verified value = 192 N.

items.stem: During an impulse-arrest test in a stage gridiron support, a stunt-rig counterweight of mass 8 kg drops freely 2 m to taut point A and extends an elastic arrest cable by 0.5 m over 0.33 s until instantaneous rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the mean upward cord force during deceleration.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 2) = 6.26 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.33 + 8(9.81) = 230 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 230 N (A).

items.stem: The diagram shows a telemetry capsule (2.2 kg) at the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 2 m in a vertical rotation stand; a high-tensile cord has a maximum safe tension of 95 N. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum allowed speed at this point?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((95/2.2) − 9.81) × 2] = 8.17 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 8.17 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: In a stage gridiron support, a stunt-rig counterweight of mass 8 kg is released from rest at the upper support of an elastic arrest cable, which has natural unstretched length 2.2 m and obeys Hooke's law when taut. The cord first becomes taut at A and reaches maximum extension 1.15 m at lowest point B after an arrest interval of 0.18 s. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance.

markScheme.criterion: Uses free-fall relation v_A = √(2gL).
Obtains 6.57 m s⁻¹.
Equates mg(L + x) = ½kx² over the complete vertical drop.
Obtains 398 N m⁻¹.
Evaluates a_B = (kx − mg) / m.
Obtains 47.3 m s⁻².

items.stem: The horizontal boom of a quarry stone-block jib crane has total length L = 15 m and mass 550 kg, supported on a vertical mast pivot P located 4.5 m from the rear end A. A concrete counterweight of mass 1800 kg sits 3.3 m to the left of P (1.2 m from A). The centre of gravity G of the boom itself lies 4 m to the right of P (8.5 m from A), and the hoist hook hangs 10 m to the right of P (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum safe load weight that can be suspended from the hook without producing a net clockwise tipping moment about P?
items.workedSolution: Anticlockwise counterweight moment about P: M_cw = 1800 × 9.81 × 3.3 = 5.827 × 10⁴ N m. Clockwise boom moment: M_boom = 550 × 9.81 × 4 = 2.158 × 10⁴ N m. Remaining clockwise moment available for load: W_max × 10 = 3.669 × 10⁴ N m ⇒ W_max = 3669 N ≈ 3.67e+3 N, m_max = W_max / 9.81 = 374.0 kg ≈ 374 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Correct maximum safe load weight = 3.67e+3 N.

items.stem: In a chute calibration, a shipyard keel block of mass 11.5 kg descends 4.5 m from rest down a dry-dock slip plank inclined at 38° and exits the base at 4.79 m s⁻¹ under constant friction. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². If the same object is instead released from rest halfway down a dry-dock slip plank, what speed does it reach at the bottom?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 38° − ½mv² = 181 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 4.5 = 40.1 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.39 m s⁻¹. Target = 3.39 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 3.39 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Along a horizontal frictionless air track, glider X of mass 1.2 kg moves to the right at 8 m s⁻¹ and strikes stationary glider Y of mass 2.9 kg. Immediately after the collision, glider Y moves to the right at 4.2 m s⁻¹. Take rightward as positive.

items.stem: Referring to the launch of a hail-impact test sphere from an angled gas gun at 42 m s⁻¹ and 28° above a horizontal test hall: Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test hall does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 28° = 37.1 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 28°)² / (2g) = 19.8 m. Target = 19.8 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 28° at apex to obtain 19.8 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: In a workshop statics test, a theatre stage lighting batten AB of length L = 4.2 m and mass 19 kg has its centre of gravity G at 2.1 m from end A. It is balanced horizontally on a knife-edge pivot P located 1.34 m from end A by placing a 28 kg calibration block to the left of P (use g = 9.81 m s⁻²). How far from end B must the 28 kg block be positioned for horizontal equilibrium?
items.workedSolution: Distance of CG from pivot P: d_G = 2.1 − 1.34 = 0.7600 m. Taking moments about P: 28 × d = 19 × 0.7600 ⇒ d = 0.5157 m left of P. Position from end A is x_A = 1.34 − 0.5157 = 0.8243 m. Therefore distance from end B is L − x_A = 4.2 − 0.8243 = 3.376 m ≈ 3.38 m.

markScheme.criterion: Correct distance from end B = 3.38 m.

items.stem: During a head-on collision test on a smooth glass collision groove, trolley X (3 kg) moves right at 11 m s⁻¹ while trolley Y (4.2 kg) moves left at 3.5 m s⁻¹ (arrow omitted), and trolley Y exits right at 3 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of trolley X right after collision.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (3)(11) + (4.2)(−3.5) = 18.3 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (3)v_X + (4.2)(3), v_X = 1.90 m s⁻¹, which is 1.90 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 18.3 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 1.90 m s⁻¹ to the right (C).

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a builder's overhanging scaffold plank of total length L = 5.8 m and mass 52 kg rests horizontally on two narrow supports A and B. Support A is positioned 0.8 m from its left end, and support B is 3 m to the right of A, leaving an unsupported right-hand overhang of 2 m. A technician of mass 70 kg initially stands 2.3 m from the left end of the plank (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). How far past support B onto the overhang can the technician walk before the plank begins to tip?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about B: F₁ × 3 = (52 × 0.9000 + 70 × 1.500) × 9.81 ⇒ F₁ = 496.4 N ≈ 496 N. At tipping (F₁ = 0): m_load × d_tip = m_beam × (x_B − x_G) ⇒ d_tip = (52 × 0.9000) / 70 = 0.6686 m ≈ 0.669 m. At the very tip (overhang 2 m): m_end = (52 × 0.9000) / 2 = 23.40 kg ≈ 23.4 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Correct solver-verified answer = 0.669 m.

items.stem: On a horizontal test hall, an angled gas gun launches a hail-impact test sphere from ground level at speed 30 m s⁻¹ and angle 26° above the horizontal. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates u_y = u sin θ.
Obtains 13.2 m s⁻¹.
Applies T = 2u_y / g.
Obtains 2.68 s.
Multiplies u cos θ by flight time T.
Obtains 72.3 m.

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, a mine-tunnel shuttle vehicle of mass 1700 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling pendulum sensor hangs at 22° to the vertical, later climbs a 12° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 50 m (static friction coefficient 0.85), and coasts from 22 m s⁻¹ against a 530 N resistive force toward the shaft station. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a ceiling pendulum sensor deflects by 22°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 22° = ma and T cos 22° = mg => a = g tan 22° = 3.96 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.85 × 9.81 × 50) = 20.4 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1700)(22)² / 530 = 776 m. Target = 3.96 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.96 m s⁻² (C).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: The force–time graph compares a rigid vehicle collision with an identical-mass car fitted with a front crumple zone stopping from the same speed. Why does the crumple zone reduce injury to occupants?
items.workedSolution: Both curves enclose equal area ($\Delta p = F\Delta t$); same change in momentum over a longer impact time reduces average force on occupants. Therefore option D is correct: same change in momentum over a longer impact time reduces average force on occupants.

markScheme.criterion: Select option D: same change in momentum over a longer impact time reduces average force on occupants.

items.stem: A uniform composite quay fender beam of length L = 2.90 m rests horizontally on level ground (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). As shown in the figure, it has a rectangular cross-section of width w = 28.0 cm and thickness h = 14.0 cm and average density ρ = 1850 kg m⁻³. The component is uniform along its length so its centre of gravity G lies at its midpoint. A dockside electric derrick rated at electrical input power 680 W and efficiency 78% is later attached to end B to stand the component vertically upright on end A.
items.workedSolution: (a) A = 0.03920 m², V = A L = 0.1137 m³, m = ρ V = 210.3 kg ≈ 210 kg. (b) W = 2063 N; taking moments about A gives F = W × (x_G / L) = 1032 N ≈ 1.03e+3 N. (c) Centre of gravity rises by Δh = 1.450 m, so ΔE_p = m g Δh = 2992 J ≈ 2.99e+3 J. (d) Useful power P_out = 0.78 × 680 = 530.4 W, so t = 2992 / 530.4 = 5.640 s ≈ 5.64 s. (e) density is uniform and negligible work is done against friction or giving kinetic energy to the beam.

markScheme.criterion: Computes cross-section A = w h = 0.03920 m² with cm → m conversion.
Calculates V = A L = 0.1137 m³ and substitutes m = ρ V.
Shows 4 s.f. mass 210.3 kg rounding clearly to 210 kg.
Applies principle of moments about A: F × 2.90 = m g × 1.450.
Evaluates minimum lift force F = 1.03e+3 N (4 s.f. 1032 N).
Uses centre-of-gravity rise Δh = 1.450 m (not full length L) in ΔE_p = m g Δh.
Obtains work done = 2.99e+3 J (4 s.f. 2992 J).
Applies useful power P_out = η P_in = 530.4 W and t = ΔE_p / P_out.
Evaluates minimum hoist time = 5.64 s (4 s.f. 5.640 s).
States valid physical assumption: density is uniform and negligible work is done against friction or giving kinetic energy to the beam.

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a broadcast-studio microphone gantry beam of total length L = 2.6 m and mass 34 kg hangs horizontally in equilibrium from two light vertical ceiling wires attached at A and B, separated by 1.9 m. Its centre of gravity G lies 1.18 m to the right of attachment A and 0.72 m to the left of attachment B (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Moments about B yield T₁ = 126.4 N ≈ 126 N. (b) Force balance gives T₂ = 207.1 N ≈ 207 N. (c) wire B carries the greater tension because the centre of gravity is closer to wire B.

markScheme.criterion: Applies moment balance about attachment B.
Applies ΣF_y = 0 to obtain T₂.
Identifies the wire closer to G as carrying greater tension.
Justifies using equal opposite moments about G with shorter lever arm.

workingSteps: Since wire A is vertical, T₁ = 126.4 N ≈ 126 N.

parts.prompt: Using vertical force equilibrium, determine the tension T₂ in wire B.
State which wire carries the greater tension and justify your answer qualitatively in terms of moments about the centre of gravity.
parts.expectedAnswer: In equilibrium, wire B carries the greater tension because the centre of gravity is closer to wire B.
workingSteps: Take moments about the centre of gravity so the weight has zero moment.
Show that the wire with the shorter perpendicular distance to G must exert the larger tension to balance moments.

items.stem: Two equal and opposite parallel forces, each of magnitude F = 134 N, are applied to the ends of a surveying-theodolite tangent lever of length d = 0.44 m, acting perpendicularly to the bar, as illustrated in the diagram.
items.workedSolution: (a) Static equilibrium requires zero resultant force and zero resultant moment about any point. (b) Torque of the couple is T = F d_perp = 58.96 N m ≈ 59.0 N m (note N m, not J).

markScheme.criterion: Zero resultant force.
Zero resultant moment about any point.
Applies T = F d_perp using perpendicular separation.
Torque = 59.0 N m with unit N m.

items.stem: A uniform rectangular a workshop hinged folding workbench flap of length L = 1.3 m and mass 6 kg is smoothly hinged along its left edge O to a vertical wall. It is held horizontally in equilibrium by a vertical upward force F applied at its outer edge 1.3 m from hinge O (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the magnitude of the vertical upward force F required at the outer edge?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about wall hinge O: F × L = m g (L / 2) ⇒ F = ½ m g = 0.5 × 6 × 9.81 = 29.43 N ≈ 29.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Correct vertical holding force F = 29.4 N.

items.workedSolution: RP4 mark-scheme principle: A long thin wire produces a larger measurable extension e for safe loads, reducing percentage uncertainty, while an identical reference wire compensates both ceiling sag and thermal expansion while orthogonal micrometer diameter measurements reduce cross sectional area uncertainty.

markScheme.criterion: A long thin wire produces a larger measurable extension e for safe loads, reducing percentage uncertainty, while an identical reference wire compensates both ceiling sag and thermal expansion while orthogonal micrometer diameter measurements reduce cross sectional area uncertainty.

options.distractorRationale: A thinner wire actually increases %Δd, which is why precise orthogonal micrometer readings are essential.

items.stem: Which SI unit name corresponds directly to angular impulse $T\Delta t$ and angular momentum $I\omega$?
items.workedSolution: Torque has unit $\text{N m}$ and time has unit $\text{s}$, so angular impulse $T\Delta t$ has SI unit $\text{N m s}$, the newton metre second.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly identifies that newton metre second.

items.stem: Engineers evaluate a composite flywheel of moment of inertia 3.10 kg m² operating between 480 rad s⁻¹ and 160 rad s⁻¹ inside a mountain-shuttle railcar of total mass 1.42e+3 kg. On a test incline of road length 260 m rising 18.0 m vertically, the mean resistive drag force is 260 N. Take $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
items.workedSolution: (a) $\Delta E_{\mathrm{k}} = 3.17 × 10⁵ J$. (b) $\Delta E_{\mathrm{p}} = 2.51 × 10⁵ J$. (c) Subtracting drag work 6.76 × 10⁴ J and dividing by $mg$ gives $h_{\max} = 17.9 m$.

markScheme.criterion: Uses $\Delta E_{\mathrm{k}} = \frac{1}{2}I(\omega_{\max}^2 - \omega_{\min}^2)$.
Obtains 3.17 × 10⁵ J.
Uses $mgh$ with $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Obtains 2.51 × 10⁵ J.
Computes drag work $F_{\mathrm{d}}s$ and subtracts from flywheel energy release.
Equates remaining energy to $mg h_{\max}$.
Obtains $h_{\max} = 17.9 m$.

parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy released by the flywheel as it slows across its operating speed range.
Calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy during the test incline.
workingSteps: Use $\Delta E_{\mathrm{p}} = m g \Delta h$ with $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.prompt: Assuming zero transmission losses and constant resistive work along the same road length, determine the maximum vertical height this flywheel energy release could lift the vehicle.
workingSteps: Work against drag $W_{\mathrm{d}} = F_{\mathrm{d}} s = 6.76 × 10⁴ J$.
Remaining energy for height gain $mgh_{\max} = \Delta E_{\mathrm{k}} - W_{\mathrm{d}}$.

items.stem: In a ballistic pendulum rig, a steel pendulum bob of mass 2 kg on a light string of length 1.6 m is released from rest with the string horizontal and coalesces at the lowest point with stationary a lump of modelling clay of mass 2.4 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above the lowest point do the joined bodies reach?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 5.60 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 2.55 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.331 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 17.1 J. Target = 0.331 m.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 0.331 m (D).

items.stem: Two wheels have identical total mass and outer diameter, but Wheel A is a solid uniform disc whereas Wheel B concentrates most of its mass in a heavy outer rim joined by thin spokes. Which statement correctly explains why Wheel B is harder to accelerate rotationally?
items.workedSolution: Because $I = \sum m r^2$, each mass element contributes in proportion to $r^2$: concentrating mass at a larger radius from the rotation axis increases moment of inertia.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly identifies that concentrating mass at a larger radius from the rotation axis increases moment of inertia.

items.stem: Starting from rest at the top of a planar timber skidway of length 10.5 m inclined at 32° to the horizontal, a quarry basalt block of mass 1.5 kg slides to the bottom where its speed is 7.94 m s⁻¹. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses ΔE_p = mgL sin θ.
Obtains 81.9 J.
Subtracts ½mv² from ΔE_p.
Obtains 34.6 J.

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a cargo-bay tapered aluminium ramp leaf of length L = 1.4 m and mass 18 kg is smoothly hinged at O to a vertical wall and held horizontally in static equilibrium. Because of an internal reinforcing frame, its centre of gravity G lies 0.59 m from hinge O. A single steel cable attached to the outer edge pulls upward and toward the wall at an angle of 26° to the vertical (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 82.80 N ≈ 82.8 N. (b) the angled wire exerts a horizontal component pulling toward the wall so the hinge must provide an equal horizontal force away from the wall for translational equilibrium. (c)(i) R_x = 36.30 N, R_y = 102.2 N, so R = 108.4 N ≈ 108 N. (c)(ii) α = tan⁻¹(R_y / R_x) = 70.44° ≈ 70.4° above the horizontal.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Στ = 0 about O using T cos(angle to vertical) × L = m g x_G.
Obtains T = 82.80 N (82.8 N) matching 83 N.
Identifies horizontal component of angled cable tension directed toward the wall.
States hinge must exert an equal opposite horizontal force away from the wall for ΣF_x = 0.
Computes R_x = 36.30 N and R_y = 102.2 N and applies Pythagoras.
Resultant hinge reaction magnitude R = 108 N.
Uses tan α = R_y / R_x with both hinge components.
Direction α = 70.4° above the horizontal.

workingSteps: Vertical component of cable tension is T cos 26°.
Equate moments about O: T cos 26° × 1.4 = 18 × 9.81 × 0.59.

parts.prompt: Explain why hinge O must exert a horizontal component of force on the door, and state its direction.
parts.expectedAnswer: For horizontal equilibrium, the angled wire exerts a horizontal component pulling toward the wall so the hinge must provide an equal horizontal force away from the wall for translational equilibrium.
workingSteps: Identify that the inclined cable pulls horizontally toward the wall.
Conclude from zero horizontal resultant force that the hinge must push horizontally away from the wall.

items.stem: Released from rest at the anchor of a stretchable nylon hawser (natural length 3.2 m) in a dry-test tower, a marine mooring weight of mass 12 kg falls freely to point A where the cord becomes taut, then stretches the cord by 0.9 m over 0.27 s before reaching instantaneous rest at B. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates v_A = √(2gL).
Obtains 7.92 m s⁻¹.
Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = m v_A, including weight mg.
Mean resultant upward force = (12 × 7.92) / 0.27 = 352 N.
Obtains 470 N.
Uses mg(L + x) = ½kx² and T_B = kx.
Obtains 1.07 × 10³ N.

items.stem: In a laboratory ceiling mount, a calibration steel ball of mass 5.5 kg is released from rest at the anchor of a Hookean rubber cord of unstretched length 3 m. The cord becomes taut at A and stretches obeying Hooke's law by a maximum extension of 0.45 m over 0.26 s before a calibration steel ball comes momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a Hookean rubber cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3 + 0.45 = 3.45 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 1.84 × 10³ N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 826 N. Target = 1.84 × 10³ N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3 + 0.45) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 1.84 × 10³ N m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The horizontal boom of an offshore-platform supply jib crane has total length L = 15 m and mass 950 kg, supported on a vertical mast pivot P located 7 m from the rear end A. A concrete counterweight of mass 3800 kg sits 5 m to the left of P (2 m from A). The centre of gravity G of the boom itself lies 2.5 m to the right of P (9.5 m from A), and the hoist hook hangs 5.5 m to the right of P (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) M_cw = 1.864 × 10⁵ N m ≈ 1.86 × 10⁵ N m. (b) Equating clockwise and anticlockwise moments about P gives m_max = 3023 kg ≈ 3.02e+3 kg. (c) Vertical force balance yields R = 7.625 × 10⁴ N ≈ 7.63 × 10⁴ N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses M = m g d with counterweight mass and lever arm from P.
Counterweight moment = 1.86 × 10⁵ N m.
Subtracts boom self-weight moment from counterweight moment and divides by g × load lever arm.
Maximum safe load mass = 3.02e+3 kg.
Applies vertical force balance summing counterweight, boom, and load weights.
Upward mast reaction R = 7.63 × 10⁴ N.

items.stem: On a frictionless optical-bench track, carriage X of mass 1.6 kg moves right at 10 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary carriage Y of mass 1.2 kg. Immediately after impact, carriage Y moves right at 7.23 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of carriage X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (1.6)(10) = (1.6)v_X + (1.2)(7.23), giving v_X = 4.58 m s⁻¹. K_i = 80.0 J and K_f = 48.1 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 31.9 J. Target = 4.58 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 4.58 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: On a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, lighter shuttle X of mass 1.4 kg moving right at 15 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier shuttle Y of mass 5 kg, causing shuttle Y to move right at 5.03 m s⁻¹ while shuttle X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1.4)(15) = (1.4)v_X + (5)(5.03) gives v_X = -2.96 m s⁻¹ (2.96 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1.4)(2.96)² + ½(5)(5.03)² = 69.4 J. Energy lost = 158 J − K_f = 88.1 J. Target = 88.1 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.96 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 88.1 J (A).

items.stem: In a vertical swing circle, a polished alloy bob of mass 0.9 kg whirls in a vertical circle of radius 0.7 m on a light suspension line and passes through the lowest point at speed 5 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the tension in a light suspension line at the lowest point?
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 0.9 × 5² / 0.7 = 32.1 N, so T = 32.1 + 0.9 × 9.8 = 41.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 41.0 N (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: Launched from a tee on flat ground across a level driving range, a golf launch-monitor ball has an initial speed of 33 m s⁻¹ at 55° above the horizontal. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) v_apex = 33 × cos 55°. Answer: 18.9 m s⁻¹. (b) u_y = 33 × sin 55° = 27.0 m s⁻¹. h_max = u_y² / (2 × 9.8). Answer: 37.3 m. (c) T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 5.52 s. R = 18.9 × T. Answer: 104 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes v_y = 0 at apex so v_apex = u cos θ.
Obtains 18.9 m s⁻¹.
Applies h_max = (u sin θ)² / (2g).
Obtains 37.3 m.
Evaluates R = u_x × (2u_y / g).
Obtains 104 m.

items.stem: On a smooth glass collision groove, trolley X of mass 4 kg moves to the right at 7 m s⁻¹ and collides head-on with trolley Y of mass 2.4 kg moving to the left at 2 m s⁻¹ (arrow on Y not shown). Immediately after impact, trolley Y moves to the right at 5 m s⁻¹. Take motion to the right as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) p_before = 4 × 7 + 2.4 × (−2) = 23.2 kg m s⁻¹. Answer: 23.2 kg m s⁻¹ to the right. (b) v_X = (23.2 − 2.4 × 5) / 4 = 2.80 m s⁻¹. Answer: 2.80 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m_X u_X − m_Y |u_Y| with correct signs.
Obtains 23.2 kg m s⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a conservatory plant-staging timber beam of total length L = 5.2 m and mass 56 kg rests horizontally on two narrow supports A and B. Support A is positioned at its left end, and support B is 3.2 m to the right of A, leaving an unsupported right-hand overhang of 2 m. A technician of mass 64 kg initially stands 0.7 m from the left end of the plank (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Moments about B give F₁ = 593.5 N ≈ 594 N. (b) Vertical equilibrium gives F₂ = 583.7 N ≈ 584 N. (c) the reaction force at support A decreases and the reaction force at support B increases. (d) Setting F₁ = 0 about B yields d_tip = 0.5250 m ≈ 0.525 m.

markScheme.criterion: Takes moments about B summing plank and technician anticlockwise moments.
Support A reaction F₁ = 594 N.
Support B reaction F₂ = 584 N via vertical force balance.
States that the reaction force at support A decreases and the reaction force at support B increases.
Sets F₁ = 0 and equates clockwise overhang moment to restoring plank moment about B.
Tipping distance past B = 0.525 m.

workingSteps: Clockwise moment of F₁ about B = F₁ × 3.2.

State qualitatively how the reaction forces at supports A and B change as the technician walks slowly toward the right-hand overhang.
parts.expectedAnswer: As the technician moves toward the overhang, the reaction force at support A decreases and the reaction force at support B increases.
workingSteps: Explain that shifting weight toward support B reduces the anticlockwise moment about B so support A carries less load while support B carries more.

parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum distance past support B that the technician can walk onto the overhang before the plank begins to tip.
workingSteps: At the tipping limit, F₁ = 0; take moments about B: 64 g d_tip = 56 g (0.6000).

items.stem: Across a flat proving ground, a calibrated ground launcher projects an acoustic ranging dart with initial speed 44 m s⁻¹ at 52° above the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a flat proving ground?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 44 sin 52° = 34.7 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 44 cos 52° = 27.1 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 7.08 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 192 m. Target = 192 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 192 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: During proving-ground tests, a harbour container carrier of mass 1300 kg accelerates along a level straight so a suspended mass indicator deflects by 22° from the vertical, climbs a straight 8° incline at constant speed, negotiates a flat semicircular curve of radius 40 m (coefficient of static friction 0.55), and finally coasts along the semicircle from 14 m s⁻¹ against a constant 470 N resistance toward the berth checkpoint. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg => a = g tan θ.
Obtains 3.96 m s⁻².
Applies μ_s mg = m v_max² / R.
Obtains 14.7 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts resistive work F_res(πR) from initial kinetic energy ½mu².
Obtains 10.3 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: By resolving forces on a suspended mass indicator, calculate the horizontal acceleration when the string deflects by 22°.
Calculate the maximum speed on the flat semicircular road without sliding.
Calculate the speed with which a harbour container carrier reaches the berth checkpoint at the end of the semicircular coast.

items.stem: A skydiver falls at constant terminal velocity where upward air drag equals downward weight. Which force forms the true Newton's third law pair with the skydiver's downward weight?
items.workedSolution: Weight is the Earth's downward gravitational pull on the skydiver; its N3L partner must be the same force type acting on the other body: the gravitational pull of the skydiver upward on the Earth. Therefore option D is correct: gravitational pull of the skydiver upward on the Earth.

markScheme.criterion: Select option D: gravitational pull of the skydiver upward on the Earth.

options.text: The Newton's third law reaction force is the upward air drag acting on the skydiver
options.distractorRationale: Classic AQA trap! Drag and weight act on the SAME body (N1L equilibrium) and are different force types (contact vs gravitational).

options.distractorRationale: Tension acts on the skydiver (same body) and is an electromagnetic contact force, not gravitational.

options.label: C
options.text: The Newton's third law reaction force is zero because the skydiver is no longer accelerating
options.distractorRationale: Newton's third law pairs always exist with equal magnitude regardless of acceleration.

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a laboratory non-uniform brass display rod of total length L = 3.6 m and mass 8 kg hangs horizontally in equilibrium from two light vertical ceiling wires attached at A and B, separated by 3.1 m. Its centre of gravity G lies 1.18 m to the right of attachment A and 1.92 m to the left of attachment B (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Without carrying out a full calculation, which statement correctly compares the tensions in the two wires?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about the centre of gravity G gives T₁ d_A = T₂ d_B, so the wire with the smaller distance to G carries the larger tension: wire A carries the greater tension because the centre of gravity is closer to wire A.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly concludes that wire A carries the greater tension because the centre of gravity is closer to wire A.

options.label: C
options.text: Wire B carries the greater tension because the centre of gravity is farther from wire B.
options.distractorRationale: Reverses the inverse lever-arm relation; the support closer to G bears the larger share of weight.
