items.stem: Two equal and opposite parallel forces, each of magnitude F = 50 N, are applied to the ends of a marine rudder control wheel bar of length d = 0.28 m, acting perpendicularly to the bar, as illustrated in the diagram. What is the magnitude of the torque of this couple?
items.workedSolution: Torque of a couple = F × perpendicular separation = 50 × 0.28 = 14.00 N m ≈ 14.0 N m.

markScheme.criterion: Correct couple torque = 14.0 N m.

items.stem: Sliding at constant velocity down a straight haulage incline of slope length 30 m and vertical drop 7.2 m, a mining equipment skid has weight 360 N. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 360 × 7.2 = 2.59 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 86.4 N. Target = 86.4 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 7.2/30 and zero net force to obtain 86.4 N (B).

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a botanical garden hanging-basket wall rod is a uniform horizontal rod of length L = 2.8 m and mass 7 kg smoothly hinged to a vertical wall at O. A rectangular sign of mass 8.5 kg hangs so that its centre of gravity acts 2.5 m from O. A taut support wire joins the outer end of the rod to the wall at an angle of 30° above the horizontal rod (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Moments about O give T = 217.6 N ≈ 218 N. (b) Horizontal balance: R_x = T cos θ = 188.4 N ≈ 188 N. (c) Vertical balance: R_y = W_total − T sin θ = 43.27 N ≈ 43.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Writes full moment balance about hinge O including both rod and sign moments with T sin θ.
Evaluates T = 217.6 N (218 N) showing agreement with 2.2e+2 N.
Applies horizontal equilibrium R_x = T cos θ.
R_x = 188 N away from the wall.
Applies vertical equilibrium R_y = W_total − T sin θ.
R_y = 43.3 N upwards.

parts.prompt: Calculate the vertical component of the force exerted by hinge O on the rod.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium: R_y = W − T sin 30° = 43.27 N ≈ 43.3 N upwards.

items.stem: Which safety measures and experimental controls are required during Searle's Young modulus investigation (RP4)?
items.workedSolution: RP4 mark-scheme principle: Wear safety goggles for snapping-wire whiplash and place a sand tray beneath slotted masses; also an identical reference wire compensates both ceiling sag and thermal expansion while orthogonal micrometer diameter measurements reduce cross sectional area uncertainty.

options.label: B
options.text: Stand directly beneath the hanging masses to read the Vernier scale vertically without parallax.
options.distractorRationale: Keep feet well clear of hanging masses above a cushioned sand tray and view the Vernier horizontally.

options.label: C
options.text: Measure wire diameter once near the ceiling clamp so the wire is not touched near the midpoint.
options.distractorRationale: Diameter must be measured in perpendicular directions at least three places along the wire.

options.label: D
options.text: Use a plastic thread as the reference wire because plastic stretches less than steel.
options.distractorRationale: The reference wire must be identical material and length to cancel thermal expansion.

items.stem: When a spinning satellite retracts its extended radial mass pods inward in deep space, its angular momentum stays constant yet its rotational kinetic energy increases. What supplies this extra rotational kinetic energy?
items.workedSolution: Since $E_{\mathrm{k}} = \frac{L^2}{2I}$ rises when $I$ decreases at constant $L$, internal radial forces do positive work pulling masses inward so rotational kinetic energy increases.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly identifies that internal radial forces do positive work pulling masses inward so rotational kinetic energy increases.

options.text: Internal radial forces do positive work pulling masses inward so rotational kinetic energy increases.

options.label: B

items.stem: Referring to the turning-moment diagram for a four-stroke engine coupled to a steady external load, how does the flywheel prevent the crankshaft from stalling between power strokes?
items.workedSolution: On the turning-moment graph, the flywheel absorbs excess energy when engine torque exceeds mean load and releases energy during zero-torque strokes (induction, compression, exhaust), keeping $\Delta\omega$ small.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly identifies that flywheel absorbs excess energy when engine torque exceeds mean load and releases energy during zero-torque strokes.

options.label: A
options.text: Flywheel increases the mean torque generated by the engine above the thermodynamic power-stroke average.
options.distractorRationale: A passive flywheel cannot create net mechanical energy or raise mean torque.

options.label: B
options.text: Flywheel eliminates the compression stroke so engine torque stays positive throughout the cycle.
options.distractorRationale: A four-stroke cylinder still requires a compression stroke regardless of flywheel inertia.

options.label: C
options.text: Flywheel absorbs excess energy when engine torque exceeds mean load and releases energy during zero-torque strokes.

options.label: D
options.text: Flywheel converts negative torque directly into electrical energy stored in the battery.
options.distractorRationale: Standard engine flywheels smooth speed mechanically via rotational kinetic energy.

items.stem: Descending a gravity-brake ramp of length 18 m and vertical drop 8.1 m at a steady speed of 2 m s⁻¹, a warehouse pallet box has weight 1400 N. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 1400 × (8.1/18) = 630 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 1.26 × 10³ W. Target = 630 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 630 N (B).

items.stem: In a laboratory swing frame, a brass impact sphere of mass 0.9 kg hangs on a 1.6 m string, is released from rest with the string horizontal, and collides inelastically at the bottom with stationary a wax capture block of mass 1.62 kg. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a brass impact sphere strikes a wax capture block?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 5.60 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 26.5 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 2.00 m s⁻¹. Target = 26.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 26.5 N (C).

Obtains 0.432 m.

items.stem: A heavy centrifuge rotor experiences a constant bearing friction torque throughout both its spin-up phase and its braking phase. How does this bearing friction torque combine with the external applied torque in each phase?
items.workedSolution: Because friction always opposes motion, bearing friction opposes rotation and acts alongside a braking torque or against a driving torque: $T_{\mathrm{drive}} - T_{\mathrm{f}} = I\alpha$ during acceleration and $T_{\mathrm{brake}} + T_{\mathrm{f}} = I|\alpha|$ during braking.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly identifies that bearing friction opposes rotation and acts alongside a braking torque or against a driving torque.

items.stem: Released from rest at the top of an inclined launchway of length 11 m inclined at 32° to the horizontal, a marine slipway cradle of mass 9 kg reaches the bottom with speed 7.8 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the coefficient of dynamic friction μ_d between a marine slipway cradle and an inclined launchway?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 32° = 514 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(9)(7.8)² = 274 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 240 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 32°)L, μ = 0.292. Target = 0.292.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 32° accurately to obtain 0.292 (A).

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a grain-silo weighted inspection trapdoor of length L = 1.6 m and mass 20 kg is smoothly hinged at O to a vertical wall and held horizontally in static equilibrium. Because of an internal reinforcing frame, its centre of gravity G lies 0.7 m from hinge O. A single steel cable attached to the outer edge pulls upward and toward the wall at an angle of 26° to the vertical (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) the angled wire exerts a horizontal component pulling toward the wall so the hinge must provide an equal horizontal force away from the wall for translational equilibrium. (b) Moments about O give T = 95.50 N ≈ 95.5 N. (c)(i) R_x = 41.87 N ≈ 41.9 N. (c)(ii) R_y = 110.4 N ≈ 110 N. (c)(iii) R = 118.0 N ≈ 118 N. (c)(iv) α = 69.23° ≈ 69.2° above horizontal.

markScheme.criterion: Notes inward horizontal component of cable tension.
States equal opposite outward hinge reaction away from wall.
Equates cable moment T cos(angle to vertical) × L with weight moment m g x_G.
T = 95.50 N (95.5 N) clearly matching 96 N.
Combines perpendicular components via R = √(R_x² + R_y²).
Applies tan α = R_y / R_x.
α = 69.2° above the horizontal.

parts.prompt: Explain why hinge O must exert a horizontal component of force on the door, and state its direction.
parts.expectedAnswer: For translational equilibrium, the angled wire exerts a horizontal component pulling toward the wall so the hinge must provide an equal horizontal force away from the wall for translational equilibrium.
workingSteps: State that the angled cable exerts an inward horizontal pull toward the wall.
Deduce that the hinge must supply an equal outward horizontal reaction away from the wall.

parts.prompt: By taking moments about hinge O, show clearly that the tension T in the steel cable is approximately 96 N.
workingSteps: Clockwise weight moment about O = 20 × 9.81 × 0.7 = 137.3 N m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the horizontal component R_x of the force exerted by hinge O.
Calculate the vertical component R_y of the force exerted by hinge O.
Hence calculate the magnitude of the total resultant hinge force R.
Determine the angle α above the horizontal at which the resultant hinge force R acts.

items.stem: Dropped from rest at the anchor in a laboratory ceiling mount, a calibration steel ball of mass 10 kg falls freely 3.6 m until a Hookean rubber cord becomes taut at A, then stretches the cord by 0.7 m over 0.18 s to come momentarily to rest at B. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the mean upward force exerted by a Hookean rubber cord between A and B?
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 3.6) = 8.40 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.18 + 10(9.8) = 565 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 565 N (A).

items.stem: In a vertical rotation stand, a telemetry capsule of mass 1.2 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 0.8 m on a high-tensile cord, which snaps if tension exceeds 33 N. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the maximum speed a telemetry capsule can have at the bottom without breaking a high-tensile cord?
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((33/1.2) − 9.81) × 0.8] = 3.76 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 3.76 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: In a cliff-sim drop frame, a mountaineering test mass of mass 10.5 kg is released from rest at the upper support of a dynamic climbing rope, which has natural unstretched length 3.6 m and obeys Hooke's law when taut. The cord first becomes taut at A and reaches maximum extension 1.15 m at lowest point B after an arrest interval of 0.18 s. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses free-fall relation v_A = √(2gL).
Obtains 8.40 m s⁻¹.
Equates mg(L + x) = ½kx² over the complete vertical drop.
Obtains 740 N m⁻¹.
Evaluates a_B = (kx − mg) / m.
Obtains 71.2 m s⁻².

items.stem: The horizontal boom of a railway freight-yard cantilever crane has total length L = 16 m and mass 1200 kg, supported on a vertical mast pivot P located 6 m from the rear end A. A concrete counterweight of mass 4200 kg sits 4 m to the left of P (2 m from A). The centre of gravity G of the boom itself lies 4.5 m to the right of P (10.5 m from A), and the hoist hook hangs 8.5 m to the right of P (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum safe load mass that can be suspended from the hook for rotational equilibrium about P?
items.workedSolution: Anticlockwise counterweight moment about P: M_cw = 4200 × 9.81 × 4 = 1.648 × 10⁵ N m. Clockwise boom moment: M_boom = 1200 × 9.81 × 4.5 = 5.297 × 10⁴ N m. Remaining clockwise moment available for load: W_max × 8.5 = 1.118 × 10⁵ N m ⇒ W_max = 1.316 × 10⁴ N ≈ 1.32 × 10⁴ N, m_max = W_max / 9.81 = 1341 kg ≈ 1.34e+3 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Correct maximum safe load mass = 1.34e+3 kg.

items.stem: Along a smooth marshalling test track, wagon X of mass 3.6 kg travels to the right at 7 m s⁻¹ and collides with stationary wagon Y of mass 1.6 kg. Immediately after impact, wagon Y moves to the right at 7.24 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies m_X u_X = m_X v_X + m_Y v_Y.
Obtains 3.78 m s⁻¹.
Sums ½m_X v_X² + ½m_Y v_Y².
Obtains 67.7 J.
Subtracts K_f from K_i = ½m_X u_X².
Obtains 20.5 J.

items.stem: On a dry-dock slip plank (8.5 m long, angled at 34° to the horizontal), a shipyard keel block of mass 6.5 kg slides from rest and attains 5.31 m s⁻¹ at the base against constant kinetic friction. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. If the same object is instead released from rest halfway down a dry-dock slip plank, what speed does it reach at the bottom?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 34° − ½mv² = 211 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 8.5 = 24.9 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.75 m s⁻¹. Target = 3.75 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 3.75 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Whirled on a high-tensile cord of length 1.3 m in a vertical rotation stand, a telemetry capsule (1.7 kg) has speed 9.5 m s⁻¹ at the bottom of its vertical circular path. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the tension in a high-tensile cord at this instant.
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 1.7 × 9.5² / 1.3 = 118 N, so T = 118 + 1.7 × 9.8 = 135 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 135 N (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: Projected from a calibrated ground launcher at 30 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 24° above a flat proving ground, an acoustic ranging dart follows a parabolic arc. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the speed of the projectile at the highest point of its trajectory?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 24° = 27.4 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 24°)² / (2g) = 7.60 m. Target = 27.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 24° at apex to obtain 27.4 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the projectile is momentarily stationary at its highest point, forgetting its constant horizontal velocity u cos θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses u sin θ instead of u cos θ for the speed at the apex.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes speed remains equal to launch speed u throughout the flight.

items.stem: In a workshop statics test, a structural aluminium inspection girder AB of length L = 3.4 m and mass 27 kg has its centre of gravity G at 1.7 m from end A. It is balanced horizontally on a knife-edge pivot P located 1.29 m from end A by placing a 16 kg calibration block to the left of P (use g = 9.81 m s⁻²). How far from end B must the 16 kg block be positioned for horizontal equilibrium?
items.workedSolution: Distance of CG from pivot P: d_G = 1.7 − 1.29 = 0.4100 m. Taking moments about P: 16 × d = 27 × 0.4100 ⇒ d = 0.6919 m left of P. Position from end A is x_A = 1.29 − 0.6919 = 0.5981 m. Therefore distance from end B is L − x_A = 3.4 − 0.5981 = 2.802 m ≈ 2.80 m.

markScheme.criterion: Correct distance from end B = 2.80 m.

items.stem: Approaching each other along a level docking-simulator rail, module X (4 kg, 10 m s⁻¹ to the right) collides head-on with module Y (3 kg, 2 m s⁻¹ to the left, arrow not shown); afterward module Y travels to the right at 5 m s⁻¹. Determine the final velocity of module X.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (4)(10) + (3)(−2) = 34.0 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (4)v_X + (3)(5), v_X = 4.75 m s⁻¹, which is 4.75 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 34.0 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 4.75 m s⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a marina boat-boarding gangplank of total length L = 6.6 m and mass 44 kg rests horizontally on two narrow supports A and B. Support A is positioned at its left end, and support B is 5 m to the right of A, leaving an unsupported right-hand overhang of 1.6 m. A technician of mass 60 kg initially stands 4.1 m from the left end of the plank (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Which statement correctly describes the mechanical condition at the exact instant the plank starts to tip clockwise about support B?
items.workedSolution: As the technician moves out onto the overhang, the clockwise moment about B increases until the plank is on the point of lifting off support A, so the upward normal reaction force at support A decreases to zero.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies that the upward normal reaction force at support A decreases to zero.

items.stem: On calm water at launch level, a deck-level launcher launches a rescue line-throwing bob from ground level at speed 44 m s⁻¹ and angle 56° above the horizontal. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates u_y = u sin θ.
Obtains 36.5 m s⁻¹.
Applies T = 2u_y / g.
Obtains 7.44 s.
Multiplies u cos θ by flight time T.
Obtains 183 m.

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an articulated test coach of mass 1800 kg accelerates horizontally so a roof-mounted plumb sphere hangs at 30° to the vertical, later climbs a 12° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 45 m (static friction coefficient 0.55), and coasts from 16 m s⁻¹ against a 380 N resistive force toward the timing gate. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the maximum speed on the flat semicircular curve of radius 45 m without skidding?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 30° = ma and T cos 30° = mg => a = g tan 30° = 5.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.55 × 9.81 × 45) = 15.6 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1800)(16)² / 380 = 606 m. Target = 15.6 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 15.6 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Computes v² = μ_s g R without taking the square root.

items.stem: Which statement lists all essential AQA criteria for two forces to constitute a Newton's third law interaction pair?
items.workedSolution: Newton's third law pairs must have equal magnitude, opposite direction, same type of force, and act on two different bodies along the same line. Therefore option A is correct: equal magnitude opposite direction same type of force acting on two different bodies.

markScheme.criterion: Select option A: equal magnitude opposite direction same type of force acting on two different bodies.

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, an airport departure-board support girder of total length L = 3.2 m and mass 10 kg hangs horizontally in equilibrium from two light ceiling wires attached at A and B (2.5 m apart), with wire An inclined at 52° above the horizontal bar. Its centre of gravity G lies 0.8 m to the right of attachment A and 1.7 m to the left of attachment B (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the tension in wire A (T₁)?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about B: T₁_y × 2.5 = 10 × 9.81 × 1.7 ⇒ T₁_y = 66.71 N, T₂_y = 31.39 N. With wire A at 52°, T₁ = T₁_y / sin 52° = 84.65 N ≈ 84.7 N, horizontal component H = T₁ cos 52° = 52.12 N, and T₂ = √(H² + T₂_y²) = 60.84 N ≈ 60.8 N.

markScheme.criterion: Correct wire tension = 84.7 N.

items.stem: Of weight 280 N, a freight container sled descends a dockyard unloading ramp at steady speed over a slope distance of 11 m through a vertical height change of 6.2 m. How much gravitational potential energy is lost over the full length of the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 280 × 6.2 = 1.74 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 158 N. Target = 1.74 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 6.2/11 and zero net force to obtain 1.74 × 10³ J (D).

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a railway-station platform indicator arm is a uniform horizontal rod of length L = 2.6 m and mass 10 kg smoothly hinged to a vertical wall at O. A rectangular sign of mass 8 kg hangs so that its centre of gravity acts 2.1 m from O. A taut support wire joins the outer end of the rod to the wall at an angle of 50° above the horizontal rod (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the vertical upward component of force exerted on the rod by hinge O?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about hinge O: T sin 50° × 2.6 = (10 × 1.3 + 8 × 2.1) × 9.81 = 292.3 N m. Hence T sin 50° = 112.4 N and T = 146.8 N ≈ 147 N. Horizontal balance: R_x = T cos 50° = 94.35 N ≈ 94.3 N. Vertical balance: R_y = (10 + 8) × 9.81 − 112.4 = 64.14 N ≈ 64.1 N.

markScheme.criterion: Correct verified value = 64.1 N.

items.stem: During Required Practical 4 on a yellow brass wire of length $L = 1.90$ m, three micrometer diameter pairs average to 0.36 mm, 0.38 mm, and 0.37 mm. The linear elastic graph of force $F$ against extension $e$ has gradient 5.7 N mm⁻¹. Determine the Young modulus $E$ in GPa.
items.workedSolution: Mean diameter $d = 0.37$ mm gives $A = \pi d^2/4 = 1.08 × 10⁻⁷ m²$. $E = L \times \mathrm{grad} / A = 101 GPa$. Percentage uncertainty $\%\Delta E = \%\Delta L + 2\%\Delta d + \%\Delta\mathrm{grad} = 0.0526 + 2(2.70) + 2.4 = 7.86%$.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly evaluates youngModulusGPa $= 101 GPa$.

items.stem: An upper clutch plate of moment of inertia 0.90 kg m² spinning freely at 50.0 rad s⁻¹ drops coaxially onto a stationary lower plate of moment of inertia 1.60 kg m² on a frictionless vertical shaft. Calculate the common angular velocity once slipping ceases.
items.workedSolution: With no external torque, $(I_1 + I_2)\omega_{\mathrm{f}} = I_1\omega_1$. Thus $\omega_{\mathrm{f}} = \frac{0.90 \times 50.0}{0.90 + 1.60} = 18.0 rad s⁻¹$.

markScheme.criterion: Common final angular velocity equals 18.0 rad s⁻¹.

items.stem: Motorsport KERS engineers favour carbon-fibre composite flywheel rims over heavier solid cast-iron discs for compact energy storage. Which physical property combination best explains this choice?
items.workedSolution: Maximum stored energy scales with $\frac{1}{2}I\omega_{\max}^2$, and hoop stress scales as $\rho r^2 \omega^2$: a high tensile strength low density composite rim maximises energy stored before bursting.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly identifies that high tensile strength low density composite rim maximises energy stored before bursting.

options.label: A
options.text: High density and low tensile strength allow slower rotation while storing greater kinetic energy.
options.distractorRationale: Low tensile strength limits safe centripetal stress and caps $\omega_{\max}$.

options.label: B
options.text: High tensile strength low density composite rim maximises energy stored before bursting.

options.label: C
options.text: Low elastic modulus increases radial expansion so the rim stores energy purely as elastic strain.
options.distractorRationale: Flywheels store rotational kinetic energy, not primarily elastic strain energy.

options.label: D
options.text: High electrical conductivity generates eddy-current braking that boosts stored energy.
options.distractorRationale: Eddy currents dissipate kinetic energy as unwanted heat.

items.stem: A foundry ingot sled (weight 900 N) slides at constant speed 5.5 m s⁻¹ down a refractory cooling chute, which is 16 m long and drops 7.2 m vertically. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 900 × (7.2/16) = 405 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 2.23 × 10³ W. Target = 405 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 405 N (B).

items.stem: Held with its 1 m light string horizontal in a suspension test gantry, an instrumented pendulum mass (0.3 kg) swings down from rest and sticks to stationary a magnetic-latch block (0.66 kg) at the lowest point. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the speed of the coupled bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 4.43 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 8.83 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.38 m s⁻¹. Target = 1.38 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Released from rest from a horizontal string position of length 1.4 m in a fracture-toughness pendulum, a hardened striker ball (0.8 kg) strikes and sticks to stationary a soft polymer target (0.96 kg) at the bottom of its arc. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. How much mechanical energy is dissipated during the sticking collision?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 5.24 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 2.38 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.289 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 5.99 J. Target = 5.99 J.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 5.99 J (A).

items.stem: Along an anodized calibration incline inclined at 40° to the horizontal, an avionics shock canister (mass 4.5 kg) slides 5 m from rest and arrives at the base travelling at 4.37 m s⁻¹. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. How much mechanical energy is dissipated against friction during the descent?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 40° = 142 J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(4.5)(4.37)² = 43.0 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 98.8 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 40°)L, μ = 0.585. Target = 98.8 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 40° accurately to obtain 98.8 J (C).

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a railway-depot signal-box inspection hatch of length L = 2.2 m and mass 28 kg is smoothly hinged at O to a vertical wall and held horizontally in static equilibrium. Because of an internal reinforcing frame, its centre of gravity G lies 0.79 m from hinge O. A single steel cable attached to the outer edge pulls upward and toward the wall at an angle of 28° to the vertical (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) the angled wire exerts a horizontal component pulling toward the wall so the hinge must provide an equal horizontal force away from the wall for translational equilibrium. (b) Moments about O give T = 111.7 N ≈ 112 N. (c)(i) R_x = 52.45 N ≈ 52.4 N. (c)(ii) R_y = 176.0 N ≈ 176 N. (c)(iii) R = 183.7 N ≈ 184 N. (c)(iv) α = 73.41° ≈ 73.4° above horizontal.

markScheme.criterion: Notes inward horizontal component of cable tension.
States equal opposite outward hinge reaction away from wall.
Equates cable moment T cos(angle to vertical) × L with weight moment m g x_G.
T = 111.7 N (112 N) clearly matching 1.1e+2 N.
Combines perpendicular components via R = √(R_x² + R_y²).
Applies tan α = R_y / R_x.
α = 73.4° above the horizontal.

parts.prompt: Explain why hinge O must exert a horizontal component of force on the door, and state its direction.
parts.expectedAnswer: For translational equilibrium, the angled wire exerts a horizontal component pulling toward the wall so the hinge must provide an equal horizontal force away from the wall for translational equilibrium.
workingSteps: State that the angled cable exerts an inward horizontal pull toward the wall.
Deduce that the hinge must supply an equal outward horizontal reaction away from the wall.

parts.prompt: By taking moments about hinge O, show clearly that the tension T in the steel cable is approximately 1.1e+2 N.
workingSteps: Clockwise weight moment about O = 28 × 9.81 × 0.79 = 217.0 N m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the horizontal component R_x of the force exerted by hinge O.
Calculate the vertical component R_y of the force exerted by hinge O.
Hence calculate the magnitude of the total resultant hinge force R.
Determine the angle α above the horizontal at which the resultant hinge force R acts.

items.stem: In an overhead hoist beam, a crane overload test block (13 kg) falls from rest at the support through the 3.4 m slack length of an elastic snubber line to point A and is brought momentarily to rest after stretching 1 m in a time of 0.24 s to B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the time-averaged tension in an elastic snubber line during this 0.24 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.81 × 3.4) = 8.17 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.24 + 13(9.81) = 570 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 570 N (D).

items.stem: Whirled in a vertical circle of radius 2.2 m on a light inextensible string (breaking tension 63 N) in a circular motion demonstrator, a polymer-coated mass has mass 1.6 kg. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. Determine the greatest safe speed at the lowest point.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((63/1.6) − 9.81) × 2.2] = 8.06 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 8.06 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: Released from rest at the support in a fall-arrest gantry, a rescue arrest dummy (11.5 kg) falls freely through the 3.4 m natural length of a braided dynamic lanyard to point A and then extends the Hookean cord by 1.15 m during 0.26 s to instantaneous rest at B. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the peak tension in a braided dynamic lanyard at the lowest point B?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 3.4 + 1.15 = 4.55 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 776 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 893 N. Target = 893 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (3.4 + 1.15) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 893 N (A).

items.stem: The horizontal boom of a hydroelectric dam maintenance crane has total length L = 22 m and mass 950 kg, supported on a vertical mast pivot P located 4.5 m from the rear end A. A concrete counterweight of mass 3000 kg sits 3.3 m to the left of P (1.2 m from A). The centre of gravity G of the boom itself lies 3.5 m to the right of P (8 m from A), and the hoist hook hangs 16 m to the right of P (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum safe load mass that can be suspended from the hook for rotational equilibrium about P?
items.workedSolution: Anticlockwise counterweight moment about P: M_cw = 3000 × 9.81 × 3.3 = 9.712 × 10⁴ N m. Clockwise boom moment: M_boom = 950 × 9.81 × 3.5 = 3.262 × 10⁴ N m. Remaining clockwise moment available for load: W_max × 16 = 6.450 × 10⁴ N m ⇒ W_max = 4031 N ≈ 4.03e+3 N, m_max = W_max / 9.81 = 410.9 kg ≈ 411 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Correct maximum safe load mass = 411 kg.

items.stem: Travelling at 12 m s⁻¹ to the right along a precision gas-bearing trough, rider X (2.8 kg) strikes stationary rider Y (2.4 kg), sending rider Y rightward at 8.18 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of rider X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (2.8)(12) = (2.8)v_X + (2.4)(8.18), giving v_X = 4.99 m s⁻¹. K_i = 202 J and K_f = 115 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 86.5 J. Target = 4.99 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 4.99 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: On a dry-dock slip plank (5.5 m long, angled at 30° to the horizontal), a shipyard keel block of mass 2.5 kg slides from rest and attains 4.77 m s⁻¹ at the base against constant kinetic friction. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. If the same object is instead released from rest halfway down a dry-dock slip plank, what speed does it reach at the bottom?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 30° − ½mv² = 39.0 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 5.5 = 7.09 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.37 m s⁻¹. Target = 3.37 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 3.37 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Moving rightward at 13 m s⁻¹ on a level cleanroom linear rail, carrier X (0.8 kg) collides head-on with stationary carrier Y (2.2 kg); immediately afterward carrier Y travels right at 6.38 m s⁻¹ and carrier X rebounds backward. What is the total kinetic energy of the two bodies immediately after impact?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (0.8)(13) = (0.8)v_X + (2.2)(6.38) gives v_X = -4.55 m s⁻¹ (4.55 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(0.8)(4.55)² + ½(2.2)(6.38)² = 53.0 J. Energy lost = 67.6 J − K_f = 14.6 J. Target = 53.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 4.55 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 53.0 J (C).

items.stem: At the bottom of a vertical circle of radius 1.9 m in a vertical whirl apparatus, a brass pendulum mass of mass 1.3 kg travels at 9.5 m s⁻¹ while attached to a taut nylon cord. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². Calculate the tension in a taut nylon cord.
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 1.3 × 9.5² / 1.9 = 61.8 N, so T = 61.8 + 1.3 × 9.8 = 74.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 74.5 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: A hail-impact test sphere leaves an angled gas gun at 15 m s⁻¹ inclined at 28° above the horizontal over a horizontal test hall. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test hall does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 28° = 13.2 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 28°)² / (2g) = 2.53 m. Target = 2.53 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 28° at apex to obtain 2.53 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a calibrated laboratory hardwood bar AB of total length L = 4.6 m and mass 12 kg is non-uniform, with its centre of gravity G located 2.48 m from end A. The beam rests horizontally in equilibrium on a sharp pivot P positioned 1.75 m from end A when a counterbalance block of unknown mass is placed 0.7 m from end A (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the upward reaction force R exerted by pivot P on the balanced beam?
items.workedSolution: Take moments about pivot P. Lever arm of beam CG is d_G = 2.48 − 1.75 = 0.7300 m. Lever arm of counterbalance is d_load = 1.75 − 0.7 = 1.050 m. Balancing moments: m_load g d_load = m_beam g d_G ⇒ m_load = (12 × 0.7300) / 1.050 = 8.343 kg ≈ 8.34 kg. Vertical equilibrium gives R = (m_beam + m_load)g = (12 + 8.343) × 9.81 = 199.6 N ≈ 200 N.

markScheme.criterion: Correct upward pivot reaction R = 200 N.

items.stem: Along a polished ice test channel, sled X of mass 2.5 kg travelling right at 13 m s⁻¹ meets sled Y of mass 3.6 kg travelling left at 2 m s⁻¹ (not drawn). After impact sled Y rebounds right at 2.5 m s⁻¹. What is the post-collision velocity of sled X?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2.5)(13) + (3.6)(−2) = 25.3 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2.5)v_X + (3.6)(2.5), v_X = 6.52 m s⁻¹, which is 6.52 m s⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = 25.3 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 6.52 m s⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a stadium camera-operator platform plank of total length L = 4.6 m and mass 36 kg rests horizontally on two narrow supports A and B. Support A is positioned 0.8 m from its left end, and support B is 2.4 m to the right of A, leaving an unsupported right-hand overhang of 1.4 m. A technician of mass 60 kg initially stands 2.5 m from the left end of the plank (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). If the technician steps off and a toolbox is placed right at the outer overhanging tip, what is the maximum toolbox mass the plank can support without tipping?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about B: F₁ × 2.4 = (36 × 0.9000 + 60 × 0.7000) × 9.81 ⇒ F₁ = 304.1 N ≈ 304 N. At tipping (F₁ = 0): m_load × d_tip = m_beam × (x_B − x_G) ⇒ d_tip = (36 × 0.9000) / 60 = 0.5400 m ≈ 0.540 m. At the very tip (overhang 1.4 m): m_end = (36 × 0.9000) / 1.4 = 23.14 kg ≈ 23.1 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Correct solver-verified answer = 23.1 kg.

items.stem: Fired from a floor-mounted spring cannon at 44 m s⁻¹ and 56° above the horizontal, a lecture-hall steel ball lands back on a level demonstration track. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the total time of flight before returning to a level demonstration track?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 44 sin 56° = 36.5 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 44 cos 56° = 24.6 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.81 = 7.44 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 183 m. Target = 7.44 s.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 7.44 s (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes time to reach the apex u sin θ / g rather than full time of flight.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps sin θ and cos θ when resolving vertical launch speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses total speed u instead of vertical component u sin θ.

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an airport baggage tractor of mass 1800 kg accelerates horizontally so a cab-mounted pendulum bob hangs at 30° to the vertical, later climbs a 12° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 55 m (static friction coefficient 0.85), and coasts from 20 m s⁻¹ against a 410 N resistive force toward the concourse stop. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻² and neglect air resistance. What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a cab-mounted pendulum bob deflects by 30°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 30° = ma and T cos 30° = mg => a = g tan 30° = 5.66 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.85 × 9.8 × 55) = 21.4 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1800)(20)² / 410 = 878 m. Target = 5.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 5.66 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: At point R on the skydiver's velocity–time graph, the parachute has just opened fully while the skydiver is still moving downwards rapidly. Which statement correctly describes the forces and motion at point R?
items.workedSolution: Opening the canopy multiplies drag above weight, giving an upward resultant force and downward deceleration. Therefore option B is correct: drag greatly exceeds weight producing an upward resultant force and downward deceleration.

markScheme.criterion: Select option B: drag greatly exceeds weight producing an upward resultant force and downward deceleration.

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a museum fossil-exhibit suspension bar of total length L = 3.8 m and mass 16 kg hangs horizontally in equilibrium from two light vertical ceiling wires attached at A and B, separated by 2.9 m. Its centre of gravity G lies 1.86 m to the right of attachment A and 1.04 m to the left of attachment B (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the tension in wire B (T₂)?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about B: T₁_y × 2.9 = 16 × 9.81 × 1.04 ⇒ T₁_y = 56.29 N, T₂_y = 100.7 N. For vertical wires, T₁ = 56.29 N ≈ 56.3 N and T₂ = 100.7 N ≈ 101 N.

markScheme.criterion: Correct wire tension = 101 N.

items.workedSolution: A couple consists of two equal and opposite parallel forces whose lines of action do not coincide.

items.stem: The diagram depicts a mining equipment skid weighing 840 N moving at constant speed down a straight haulage incline of length 11 m and vertical height 5.7 m. What is the magnitude of the resistive force opposing motion along the slope?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed ΔE_k = 0. Potential energy lost = W h = 840 × 5.7 = 4.79 × 10³ J. Parallel equilibrium gives F_res = W sin θ = W h / L = 435 N. Target = 435 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ = 5.7/11 and zero net force to obtain 435 N (C).

items.stem: As shown in the diagram, a bookshop hanging-sign bracket bar is a uniform horizontal rod of length L = 2.6 m and mass 11 kg smoothly hinged to a vertical wall at O. A rectangular sign of mass 7 kg hangs so that its centre of gravity acts 2.4 m from O. A taut support wire joins the outer end of the rod to the wall at an angle of 36° above the horizontal rod (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the tension T in the angled support wire?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about hinge O: T sin 36° × 2.6 = (11 × 1.3 + 7 × 2.4) × 9.81 = 305.1 N m. Hence T sin 36° = 117.3 N and T = 199.6 N ≈ 200 N. Horizontal balance: R_x = T cos 36° = 161.5 N ≈ 162 N. Vertical balance: R_y = (11 + 7) × 9.81 − 117.3 = 59.24 N ≈ 59.2 N.

markScheme.criterion: Correct verified value = 200 N.

items.stem: In Searle's dual-wire apparatus (RP4), why is an identical unstressed reference wire suspended beside the test wire from the same ceiling beam?
items.workedSolution: RP4 mark-scheme principle: An identical reference wire compensates both ceiling sag and thermal expansion while orthogonal micrometer diameter measurements reduce cross sectional area uncertainty.

markScheme.criterion: An identical reference wire compensates both ceiling sag and thermal expansion while orthogonal micrometer diameter measurements reduce cross sectional area uncertainty.

options.label: A
options.text: The reference wire doubles the cross-sectional area so the test wire can support twice the load.
options.distractorRationale: The slotted masses load only the test wire; the reference wire carries a small constant straightening weight.

options.label: B
options.text: An identical reference wire compensates both ceiling sag and thermal expansion while orthogonal micrometer diameter measurements reduce cross sectional area uncertainty.

options.label: C
options.text: The reference wire compensates ceiling sag only and has no effect on room-temperature drift.
options.distractorRationale: Because both wires are the same metal and length, thermal expansion shifts both scales identically so Δe is unaffected.

options.label: D
options.text: The reference wire prevents the test wire from exceeding its elastic limit during unloading.
options.distractorRationale: Checking elastic recovery requires unloading readings, not the reference wire.

items.stem: A spin-stabilised research satellite with extended sensor booms has moment of inertia 24.0 kg m² and spins at 2.20 rad s⁻¹ in deep space. Internal winches retract the booms, lowering its moment of inertia to 8.80 kg m². Calculate the new angular speed of the satellite.
items.workedSolution: By conservation of angular momentum $I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$, $\omega_2 = \frac{24.0 \times 2.20}{8.80} = 6.00 rad s⁻¹$.

markScheme.criterion: New angular speed equals 6.00 rad s⁻¹.

items.stem: A high-speed stationary flywheel energy-storage unit spins at several thousand radians per second inside a sealed housing. Which design pairing best minimises energy losses while maximising safe energy capacity?
items.workedSolution: To store energy efficiently at ultra-high $\omega$, an evacuated casing and magnetic bearings minimise windage and friction losses while high-strength rim permits greater angular speed.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly identifies that evacuated casing and magnetic bearings minimise windage and friction losses while high-strength rim permits greater angular speed.

options.label: A
options.text: Pressurised air cooling and greased steel ball bearings with a heavy lead hub.
options.distractorRationale: Pressurised air causes severe windage drag and lead has low tensile strength.

options.label: B
options.text: Open-air spoked housing with oil-bath bearings and soft aluminium spokes.
options.distractorRationale: Open-air spokes cause huge aerodynamic drag and oil churning losses.

options.label: C
options.text: Water-filled containment jacket with solid brass cylinder rotating at low speed.
options.distractorRationale: Fluid drag in water would immediately dissipate rotational energy.

options.label: D
options.text: Evacuated casing and magnetic bearings minimise windage and friction losses while high-strength rim permits greater angular speed.

items.stem: The diagram shows a warehouse pallet box of weight 850 N moving at constant speed 6 m s⁻¹ down a gravity-brake ramp of slope length 22 m and height 13.2 m. What is the magnitude of the friction force acting up the ramp?
items.workedSolution: At constant speed, friction balances downslope weight: F_f = W(h/L) = 850 × (13.2/22) = 510 N. Rate of thermal energy generation P = F_f v = 3.06 × 10³ W. Target = 510 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F_f = Wh/L and P = F_f v to obtain 510 N (B).

items.stem: The diagram shows a brass impact sphere of mass 2.3 kg released from a horizontal 0.8 m string in a laboratory swing frame toward stationary a wax capture block of mass 5.06 kg at the bottom. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string immediately before a brass impact sphere strikes a wax capture block?
items.workedSolution: Just before collision u² = 2gL => u = 3.96 m s⁻¹. Radial Newton second law T − mg = mu²/L = 2mg gives T = 3mg = 67.7 N. Momentum conservation gives v = mu/(m+M) = 1.24 m s⁻¹. Target = 67.7 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates quarter-swing dynamics and radial/tangential laws to obtain 67.7 N (B).

options.distractorRationale: Evaluates combined static weight (m + M)g rather than pre-collision string tension.

items.stem: In a ballistic pendulum rig, a steel pendulum bob of mass 0.4 kg on a light string of length 1.1 m is released from rest with the string horizontal and coalesces at the lowest point with stationary a lump of modelling clay of mass 0.32 kg. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above the lowest point do the joined bodies reach?
items.workedSolution: Pre-impact speed u = √(2gL) = 4.64 m s⁻¹. Tangential momentum conservation gives v = mu / (m + M) = 2.58 m s⁻¹. Post-impact rise h = v² / (2g) = (m/(m+M))² L = 0.340 m; energy lost = mgL − (m+M)gh = 1.92 J. Target = 0.340 m.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves energy during swings and momentum during impact to obtain 0.340 m (C).

items.stem: An industrial grinding rotor initially spinning at 18.0 rev s⁻¹ decelerates uniformly to rest in 15.0 s once its brake caliper engages. How many complete revolutions does the rotor make while slowing to a stop?
items.workedSolution: Average rotational frequency is $\bar{f} = \frac{18.0 + 0}{2} = 9.00\text{ rev s}^{-1}$. Total revolutions $N = \frac{\theta}{2\pi} = \bar{f}t = 9.00 \times 15.0 = 135 rev$.

markScheme.criterion: Rotor completes 135 rev while decelerating to rest.

items.stem: During a surface-wear test on a compacted snow test slope (11.5 m long, 44° above the horizontal), an alpine supply sled of mass 13.5 kg slides from rest to a bottom speed of 6.51 m s⁻¹. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². How much mechanical energy is dissipated against friction during the descent?
items.workedSolution: Gravitational potential energy lost ΔE_p = mgL sin 44° = 1.06 × 10³ J. Final kinetic energy E_k = ½(13.5)(6.51)² = 286 J. Frictional energy loss W_f = ΔE_p − E_k = 772 J. Since W_f = μ(mg cos 44°)L, μ = 0.705. Target = 772 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p − E_k and normal reaction mg cos 44° accurately to obtain 772 J (D).

items.stem: As shown in the figure, an observatory dome shutter baffle panel of length L = 1.6 m and mass 16 kg is smoothly hinged at O to a vertical wall and held horizontally in static equilibrium. Because of an internal reinforcing frame, its centre of gravity G lies 0.64 m from hinge O. A single steel cable attached to the outer edge pulls upward and toward the wall at an angle of 44° to the vertical (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) the angled wire exerts a horizontal component pulling toward the wall so the hinge must provide an equal horizontal force away from the wall for translational equilibrium. (b) Moments about O give T = 87.28 N ≈ 87.3 N. (c)(i) R_x = 60.63 N ≈ 60.6 N. (c)(ii) R_y = 94.18 N ≈ 94.2 N. (c)(iii) R = 112.0 N ≈ 112 N. (c)(iv) α = 57.23° ≈ 57.2° above horizontal.

markScheme.criterion: Notes inward horizontal component of cable tension.
States equal opposite outward hinge reaction away from wall.
Equates cable moment T cos(angle to vertical) × L with weight moment m g x_G.
T = 87.28 N (87.3 N) clearly matching 87 N.
Combines perpendicular components via R = √(R_x² + R_y²).
Applies tan α = R_y / R_x.
α = 57.2° above the horizontal.

parts.prompt: Explain why hinge O must exert a horizontal component of force on the door, and state its direction.
parts.expectedAnswer: For translational equilibrium, the angled wire exerts a horizontal component pulling toward the wall so the hinge must provide an equal horizontal force away from the wall for translational equilibrium.
workingSteps: State that the angled cable exerts an inward horizontal pull toward the wall.
Deduce that the hinge must supply an equal outward horizontal reaction away from the wall.

parts.prompt: By taking moments about hinge O, show clearly that the tension T in the steel cable is approximately 87 N.
workingSteps: Clockwise weight moment about O = 16 × 9.81 × 0.64 = 100.5 N m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the horizontal component R_x of the force exerted by hinge O.
Calculate the vertical component R_y of the force exerted by hinge O.
Hence calculate the magnitude of the total resultant hinge force R.
Determine the angle α above the horizontal at which the resultant hinge force R acts.

items.stem: During an impulse-arrest test in a vertical deceleration shaft, a payload shock capsule of mass 6 kg drops freely 2.6 m to taut point A and extends a compliant elastomer rope by 0.5 m over 0.33 s until instantaneous rest at B. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.8 m s⁻². Calculate the mean upward cord force during deceleration.
items.workedSolution: Speed when taut at A: v_A = √(2 × 9.8 × 2.6) = 7.14 m s⁻¹ downward. Taking upward positive, (F_mean − mg)Δt = 0 − (−mv_A), so F_mean = mv_A / 0.33 + 6(9.8) = 189 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies (F_mean − mg)Δt = mv_A with v_A = √(2gL) to obtain 189 N (D).

items.stem: During a tensile limit test in a lecture-hall whirl rig, a calibration ball of mass 1.4 kg swings on a thin braided string of length 1.2 m rated to 33 N maximum tension. Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the maximum speed at the bottom of the path.
items.workedSolution: Tension is greatest at the bottom where T_max − mg = m v_max² / r. Thus v_max = √[((33/1.4) − 9.81) × 1.2] = 4.06 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves T_max − mg = mv²/r to obtain 4.06 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds g instead of subtracting g when rearranging T_max − mg = mv²/r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats vertical circular motion as horizontal, omitting weight mg at the lowest point.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes minimum top-of-loop critical speed √(gr) instead of maximum safe bottom speed.

items.stem: The three-stage diagram shows a calibration steel ball of mass 10 kg dropped from rest at the support of a Hookean rubber cord (natural length 2.4 m), reaching A taut and extending a further 0.85 m over 0.24 s to rest at lowest point B. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the spring constant of a Hookean rubber cord?
items.workedSolution: Total vertical drop from release S to lowest point B is L + x = 2.4 + 0.85 = 3.25 m. By energy conservation mg(L + x) = ½kx², giving k = 2mg(L + x)/x² = 882 N m⁻¹ and peak tension T_B = kx = 749 N. Target = 882 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses full vertical drop (2.4 + 0.85) m in mg(L + x) = ½kx² to obtain 882 N m⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: The horizontal boom of a wind-turbine nacelle assembly crane has total length L = 18 m and mass 400 kg, supported on a vertical mast pivot P located 7 m from the rear end A. A concrete counterweight of mass 3200 kg sits 5.6 m to the left of P (1.4 m from A). The centre of gravity G of the boom itself lies 4.5 m to the right of P (11.5 m from A), and the hoist hook hangs 9 m to the right of P (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum safe load weight that can be suspended from the hook without producing a net clockwise tipping moment about P?
items.workedSolution: Anticlockwise counterweight moment about P: M_cw = 3200 × 9.81 × 5.6 = 1.758 × 10⁵ N m. Clockwise boom moment: M_boom = 400 × 9.81 × 4.5 = 1.766 × 10⁴ N m. Remaining clockwise moment available for load: W_max × 9 = 1.581 × 10⁵ N m ⇒ W_max = 1.757 × 10⁴ N ≈ 1.76 × 10⁴ N, m_max = W_max / 9.81 = 1791 kg ≈ 1.79e+3 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Correct maximum safe load weight = 1.76 × 10⁴ N.

items.stem: The diagram shows carriage X of mass 5.2 kg moving right at 5 m s⁻¹ toward stationary carriage Y of mass 1.2 kg on a frictionless optical-bench track; after collision, carriage Y travels right at 6.07 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of carriage X immediately after the collision?
items.workedSolution: Momentum conservation: (5.2)(5) = (5.2)v_X + (1.2)(6.07), giving v_X = 3.60 m s⁻¹. K_i = 65.0 J and K_f = 55.8 J, so ΔK_lost = K_i − K_f = 9.21 J. Target = 3.60 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Conserves linear momentum and evaluates kinetic energy budget to obtain 3.60 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The diagram illustrates a battery transport case (9.5 kg) released from rest at the top of a textured service ramp of length 5 m and angle 30°, arriving at the bottom at 4.55 m s⁻¹. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the magnitude of the constant friction force opposing its motion?
items.workedSolution: Energy dissipated W_f = mgL sin 30° − ½mv² = 135 J. Constant friction force F_f = W_f / 5 = 26.9 N. Released halfway down at unchanged acceleration a, v_half = v / √2 = 3.22 m s⁻¹. Target = 26.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies work-energy / constant-acceleration scaling on the incline to obtain 26.9 N (A).

items.stem: On a precision gas-bearing trough, lighter rider X of mass 1 kg moving right at 7 m s⁻¹ strikes stationary heavier rider Y of mass 3.2 kg, causing rider Y to move right at 2.82 m s⁻¹ while rider X rebounds to the left. How much kinetic energy is dissipated in this rebound collision?
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward positive, (1)(7) = (1)v_X + (3.2)(2.82) gives v_X = -2.02 m s⁻¹ (2.02 m s⁻¹ to the left). Scalar final kinetic energies add: K_f = ½(1)(2.02)² + ½(3.2)(2.82)² = 14.8 J. Energy lost = 24.5 J − K_f = 9.73 J. Target = 9.73 J.

markScheme.criterion: Finds rebound speed 2.02 m s⁻¹ and sums scalar kinetic energies to obtain 9.73 J (B).

items.stem: In a vertical circular test rig, a steel sensor sphere of mass 1.7 kg whirls in a vertical circle of radius 0.9 m on a light inextensible wire and passes through the lowest point at speed 4.5 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the tension in a light inextensible wire at the lowest point?
items.workedSolution: At the bottom, upward resultant force T − mg = mv²/r. Centripetal force mv²/r = 1.7 × 4.5² / 0.9 = 38.2 N, so T = 38.2 + 1.7 × 9.8 = 54.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = m(v²/r + g) at the bottom of the circle to obtain 54.9 N (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts weight mg instead of adding mg, confusing the bottom of a vertical circle with the top.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates tension directly to centripetal force mv²/r and forgets the downward weight mg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Sets tension equal to static weight mg, ignoring centripetal acceleration.

items.stem: Referring to the launch of a hail-impact test sphere from an angled gas gun at 36 m s⁻¹ and 33° above a horizontal test hall: Take the acceleration of free fall to be g = 9.81 m s⁻². What maximum vertical height above a horizontal test hall does it reach?
items.workedSolution: At the apex v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains constant at v_apex = u cos 33° = 30.2 m s⁻¹. Maximum height h_max = (u sin 33°)² / (2g) = 19.6 m. Target = 19.6 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_y = 0 and constant v_x = u cos 33° at apex to obtain 19.6 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Converts all initial kinetic energy into gravitational potential energy, forgetting non-zero horizontal speed u cos θ at the apex.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses horizontal component u cos θ instead of vertical component u sin θ in h = u_y² / (2g).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of two in the denominator of h_max = u_y² / (2g).

items.stem: In a workshop statics test, a botanical conservatory walkway beam AB of length L = 2.8 m and mass 10 kg has its centre of gravity G at 1.4 m from end A. It is balanced horizontally on a knife-edge pivot P located 0.84 m from end A by placing a 12 kg calibration block to the left of P (use g = 9.81 m s⁻²). How far from end B must the 12 kg block be positioned for horizontal equilibrium?
items.workedSolution: Distance of CG from pivot P: d_G = 1.4 − 0.84 = 0.5600 m. Taking moments about P: 12 × d = 10 × 0.5600 ⇒ d = 0.4667 m left of P. Position from end A is x_A = 0.84 − 0.4667 = 0.3733 m. Therefore distance from end B is L − x_A = 2.8 − 0.3733 = 2.427 m ≈ 2.43 m.

markScheme.criterion: Correct distance from end B = 2.43 m.

items.stem: During a head-on collision test on a horizontal magnetic-bearing guideway, shuttle X (2.5 kg) moves right at 5 m s⁻¹ while shuttle Y (2.4 kg) moves left at 6 m s⁻¹ (arrow omitted), and shuttle Y exits right at 4 m s⁻¹. Find the velocity of shuttle X right after collision.
items.workedSolution: Taking rightward as positive: p_before = (2.5)(5) + (2.4)(−6) = -1.90 kg m s⁻¹. From p_before = (2.5)v_X + (2.4)(4), v_X = -4.60 m s⁻¹, which is 4.60 m s⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Uses signed head-on momentum p_before = -1.90 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 4.60 m s⁻¹ to the left (A).

items.stem: As shown in the figure, a civil-lab steel overhanging girder of total length L = 5.2 m and mass 60 kg rests horizontally on two narrow supports A and B. Support A is positioned 0.8 m from its left end, and support B is 2.6 m to the right of A, leaving an unsupported right-hand overhang of 1.8 m. A technician of mass 84 kg initially stands 2.3 m from the left end of the plank (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Which statement correctly describes how the two upward support reaction forces change as the technician walks steadily from support A toward the overhanging end?
items.workedSolution: Taking moments about B shows that reducing the technician's anticlockwise lever arm lowers F₁; because F₁ + F₂ equals total weight, the reaction force at support A decreases and the reaction force at support B increases.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies that the reaction force at support A decreases and the reaction force at support B increases.

options.label: C

options.distractorRationale: Any rightward shift immediately transfers vertical load from support A to support B.

items.stem: The diagram shows a golf launch-monitor ball launched at 26 m s⁻¹ inclined at 56° to a level driving range. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What horizontal range does it cover before landing on a level driving range?
items.workedSolution: u_y = 26 sin 56° = 21.6 m s⁻¹ and u_x = 26 cos 56° = 14.5 m s⁻¹. Flight time T = 2u_y / 9.8 = 4.40 s; horizontal range R = u_x T = 64.0 m. Target = 64.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves orthogonal components accurately to obtain 64.0 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies horizontal speed by ascent time u sin θ / g instead of full flight time 2u sin θ / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cos θ for sin θ in the flight-time expression.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the 45° maximum-range formula u²/g without the angle factor sin(2θ).

items.stem: During multi-stage proving trials, an instrumented test truck of mass 1800 kg accelerates horizontally so a ceiling-suspended plumb bob hangs at 18° to the vertical, later climbs a 14° grade at steady speed, traverses a flat semicircular bend of radius 45 m (static friction coefficient 0.55), and coasts from 15 m s⁻¹ against a 410 N resistive force toward the terminal bay. Assume gravitational field strength g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the horizontal acceleration during the initial straight-line phase when a ceiling-suspended plumb bob deflects by 18°?
items.workedSolution: Plumb-bob equilibrium: T sin 18° = ma and T cos 18° = mg => a = g tan 18° = 3.18 m s⁻². Flat curve limit: v_max = √(0.55 × 9.8 × 45) = 15.6 m s⁻¹. Coasting stop distance: s = ½(1800)(15)² / 410 = 494 m. Target = 3.18 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates target vehicle mechanics relation cleanly to obtain 3.18 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses g sin θ as if on an inclined plane rather than resolving T sin θ = ma and T cos θ = mg to obtain g tan θ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio of horizontal to vertical components, evaluating g / tan θ instead of g tan θ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies g by cos θ instead of tan θ.

items.stem: A $1250\text{ kg}$ test vehicle travelling at $16.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is brought uniformly to rest in $0.400\text{ s}$ by its front crumple zone. Calculate the average stopping force exerted on the vehicle.
items.workedSolution: $\Delta p = 1250 \times 16.0 = 2.00 \times 10^4\text{ N s}$; average force $F = \Delta p / \Delta t = 2.00 \times 10^4 / 0.400 = 5.00 × 10⁴ N$. Option C (5.00 × 10⁴ N) matches.

markScheme.criterion: Average stopping force $= 5.00 × 10⁴ N$ (5.00 × 10⁴ N, option C).
